stories.title: 167K Michiganders fell off SNAP since last summer

Four people were in a Jeep Grand Cherokee when a passing vehicle opened fire, according to police.

stories.title: A quarter of Michigan teachers are considering leaving in a year
stories.summary: A poll conducted from May 29 to June 30 found that 25% of Michigan teachers are considering leaving the profession within a year, citing inadequate compensation, lack of training for new teachers, and barriers to classroom innovation. The survey, conducted by Impact Research, revealed mixed sentiments about working conditions and compensation across all teacher experience levels.

stories.title: Abdul El-Sayed releases plan to rein in AI. Mike Rogers hasn’t gone quite that far.
stories.summary: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has proposed a plan to sharply curtail AI development, including banning recursive self-improvement and establishing safety safeguards. His Republican opponent Mike Rogers advocates for a 'slowdown' in AI development but has not detailed specific measures. El-Sayed's plan includes a pause on powerful AI systems, mandatory 'kill switches,' and a cabinet-level AI safety agency, while Rogers emphasizes accelerating AI innovation with national frameworks.

stories.title: Advocates pressure lawmakers to end fees for serving restraining orders
stories.summary: Supporters of domestic violence survivors are urging Michigan lawmakers to eliminate fees for serving personal protection orders (PPOs). Currently, law enforcement agencies in Michigan can charge petitioners for PPO service, a practice found in fewer than 10 states. Advocates highlight disparities in costs across counties and a tragic case where a woman was killed after her PPO was not served. Legislation to create a state fund covering service costs has advanced in both the Senate and House, but advocates fear time is running out before the election.

stories.title: Amish teen dies after horse-drawn wagon overturns in crash

The event featured self-guided tours, historical insights into Black achievements in the community, and remarks from local leaders emphasizing the neighborhood’s legacy. Dunbar Tower is the first of several city-owned sites being developed as affordable housing projects.

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power debates DTE-backed group over ballot proposal
stories.summary: The League of Women Voters of Washtenaw County hosted a forum where Ann Arbor for Public Power (A2P2) and the DTE-backed Ann Arbor Responsible Energy Coalition (A2REC) debated their cases for a public power transition. The proposal, appearing as City Proposal E on the November 3 ballot, would establish a public utility board to oversee a potential shift from DTE Energy to city-run power by 2028. A2P2 argues for local accountability, while A2REC warns against politicizing critical infrastructure and highlights workforce concerns.

The measure, City Proposal E, would require a public utility board by 2028 and faces opposition from some local officials and labor groups over concerns about costs, expertise, and reliability. Proponents argue it would enable faster renewable energy adoption and local accountability.

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power’s ballot proposal will be in voters’ hands in November — here’s what to know
stories.summary: Ann Arbor for Public Power successfully gathered over 5,000 signatures to place a proposal on the 2026 midterm ballot, aiming to replace DTE Energy’s electrical utility with a city-run power grid. If approved on Nov. 3, a public utility board would be elected by 2028 to oversee the transition. The proposal faces opposition from DTE-funded groups, but court challenges to block it have been dismissed. Supporters argue for democratic control of utilities, while critics raise concerns about costs and grid reliability.

photo.alt: An illustration of an electric tower with a stormy background.

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power’s ballot proposal will be in voters’ hands in November — here’s what to know

If approved, voters would elect a public utility board by 2028 to guide a transition to collective ownership. The proposal faces opposition from DTE-funded groups and concerns about costs, while supporters argue it could improve climate action and grid reliability.

stories.title: Ann Arbor gathers resident feedback on city carbon offset efforts
stories.summary: The city of Ann Arbor held an interactive discussion on its carbon neutrality goals and climate action projects, in collaboration with Earthly and Austin's Office of Climate Action and Resilience. The event, part of the A2ZERO plan aiming for carbon neutrality by 2030, included public forums and a survey to gather resident input on carbon offset strategies. Speakers emphasized the importance of carbon credits and local impact in addressing climate change.

stories.title: Ann Arbor hospital earns national recognition for physician well-being
stories.summary: Trinity Health Ann Arbor and IHA Medical Group received silver-level recognition from the American Medical Association as a Joy in Medicine organization, highlighting their commitment to reducing physician burnout and supporting professional fulfillment. The health system is one of only eight in Michigan to earn the designation and the only one recognized alongside its integrated medical group. The AMA's program honors organizations that prioritize proven methods to reduce burnout and enhance professional satisfaction through documented efforts in commitment, assessment, leadership, and practice environment efficiency.

stories.title: Ann Arbor launches community-owned solar utility with battery backup
stories.summary: Ann Arbor is launching a new municipal utility using locally generated solar power and battery storage to provide residents with an optional clean energy solution. The Ann Arbor Sustainable Energy Utility (SEU) began installations in the Bryant neighborhood this year and plans to expand the community-owned program across the city in 2027.

stories.title: Ann Arbor launches community-owned solar utility with battery backup
stories.summary: Ann Arbor has launched a community-owned solar utility (SEU) that finances, installs, and maintains solar and battery systems for residents and businesses. Customers pay a monthly fee based on their system size, with savings on traditional utility bills expected to range from $100 to $300 annually. Voters authorized the program in November 2024, and the city describes it as an optional municipal utility providing 100% local renewable energy.

stories.title: Ann Arbor Marathon and Tech Trek event get city’s OK to take over streets
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Marathon and Tech Trek event received city approval to take over streets on October 2 and 4, 2026. The marathon, organized by Epic Races LLC, includes a full marathon, half marathon, 5K, 10K, and kids' run. The Tech Trek, a street fair with over 60 companies showcasing innovations, will take place downtown along Liberty Street. Both events were unanimously approved by City Council on September 22, 2026.

stories.title: Ann Arbor municipal workers’ union clashes with city over contract provisions
stories.summary: The city of Ann Arbor and AFSCME Local 369 have been in mediation since July 2025 over a new labor contract, with nearly 300 municipal workers operating without a contract since December 2025. The union demands wage increases, shift premiums, and full-time union leadership, while the city cites financial constraints. Union members criticize recent police department budget allocations as evidence of available funds, and negotiations remain unresolved with no clear timeline for resolution.

The event on the University of Michigan Diag featured discussions on cannabis, mushrooms, and their role in enhancing later life. Rosner shared her journey of rediscovering psychedelics in her 50s and highlighted how older adults are using these substances for healing, spiritual connection, and improved well-being.

stories.title: Ann Arbor saw foot traffic increase last year, new report shows

The report also noted an 11% rise in pedestrian traffic but highlighted that employee visits have not returned to pre-pandemic levels. New residential construction and rising cost of living were also discussed as factors shaping the city's economic landscape.

stories.title: Ann Arbor Teacher Contracts — What Comes Next
stories.summary: After 251 days without a contract, the Ann Arbor Public School’s Board of Education ratified a tentative agreement ending teacher protests over pay, healthcare, and class sizes. The agreement, rejected initially by the teachers' union on April 27, 2026, includes cumulative pay raises of 3-7% and will expire on December 31, 2027, with negotiations expected to resume in 2027. The process caused disruptions like late grading and canceled clubs during the 2025-2026 school year.

stories.title: Ann Arbor teachers rally before Board of Education meeting

AAPS Superintendent Jazz Parks emphasized continued collaboration with the Ann Arbor Education Association (AAEA) to reach a contract agreement, while community members called for transparency in district spending and solutions to address rising transportation and healthcare costs.

Hudson currently serves as a James S. Jackson collegiate professor and chair of health behavior and health equity in the School of Public Health.

stories.title: Arab American group ACCESS aims for a 2027 Dearborn mental health facility opening
stories.summary: Arab American Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS) is building a $25 million mental health and recovery center in Dearborn. The facility will open in phases starting in 2027 and will offer outpatient treatment, urgent care, withdrawal management, and residential beds. It will also include an on-site food pantry.

stories.title: Arab American Women’s Business Council to host a Nov. networking and pitch event
stories.summary: The Arab American Women’s Business Council (AAWBC) is hosting a pitch competition on Nov. 19, 2026 from 5:30-8 p.m. to encourage innovation and entrepreneurship among local business owners. Participants will compete for seed funding, with the event also serving as a networking opportunity. More details are available on the event’s information page.

stories.title: Arbor South development granted $110.7 million in state incentives
stories.summary: The Michigan Strategic Fund approved a $110.7 million brownfield incentive package for the Arbor South development, enabling construction to begin this year. The $651 million project will include over 1,000 housing units (200 affordable), a hotel, commercial/retail space, and improved public transportation. Ann Arbor's Economic Development Director Joe Giant emphasized the approval's importance for school district compensation and project viability.

photo.alt: Rendering of the proposed Arbor South housing complex in Ann Arbor.

stories.summary: The article provides the dates when fall foliage begins to change in different regions of Michigan according to Explore Fall's 2026 map: Western Upper Peninsula on Sept. 16, Eastern Upper Peninsula on Sept. 22, Northern Lower Peninsula on Sept. 28, and Southern Lower Peninsula on Oct. 2.

stories.title: Are some police targeting immigrants? A closer look at one jaywalking stop
stories.summary: Stopping someone based on their race or language is generally not considered legal. But police can use minor violations, like tinted car windows or jaywalking, to hide their real reasons for stopping people.

stories.title: Are woolly bears venomous or poisonous?
stories.summary: Woolly bear caterpillars are harmless and do not sting or bite, according to Vulcan Termite & Pest Control Inc. They have 13 body segments, molt six times before adulthood, and can travel up to 4 feet per minute. Their hairy coat provides insulation, and they produce sounds for mating or deterring predators.

photo.alt: Are woolly bears venomous or poisonous?

stories.title: Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here's how to check ahead of November general election
stories.summary: Michigan’s November General Election is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with early voting beginning on Oct. 24. Voters can check registration status, polling locations, and absentee-ballot details through the Michigan Voter Information Center. Registration options include online, mail, Secretary of State offices, or local clerks, with a 14-day deadline before the election for in-person registration with proof of residency.

photo.alt: Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here's how to check ahead of November general election

stories.title: Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here's how to check ahead of November general election

stories.title: Are you too old to rake leaves? Why it may be better to leave them
stories.summary: Experts warn that raking leaves can pose significant health risks, particularly for older adults or those with heart conditions, as the physical exertion may trigger heart attacks or injuries. Medical professionals advise starting slowly and avoiding sudden intense yard work, while environmental experts suggest leaving leaves to decompose naturally for ecological benefits.
entities: SIU Center for Environmental Health & Safety
Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy

stories.title: ARPA Funds May Be Reallocated to Public Health and Safety Departments if Expenditure Deadlines Are Missed
stories.summary: The state budget director may reallocate ARPA funds to public health and safety departments (corrections and state police) if deadlines are not met. Reallocations must follow ARPA guidance and notify legislative committees within 10 business days.

stories.title: Arson investigation leads to 30 child sexual abuse charges against Harrison Township man
stories.summary: A Macomb County man is facing 30 criminal sexual conduct charges after detectives allegedly found evidence of child sexual abuse on his phone during an unrelated arson investigation in September 2025. Robert Fitz, 48, of Harrison Township, was initially arraigned in June on 20 counts, with additional charges added later. He is scheduled to appear in court on September 28 for a probable cause conference.

photo.alt: Robert Fitz, 48, of Harrison Township, has been charged with 30 criminal sexual conduct charges after investigators allege finding evidence of child sexual abuse on his phone.

stories.title: Art at Work: Understanding America's Past, Shaping Public Policy's Future
stories.summary: The exhibition 'We Hold These Truths' at UMMA's Lizzie and Jonathan Tisch Apse explores the intersection of art and public policy through workshops and public dialogue. Artist Bass, during her Towsley Policymaker residency at the Ford School, will teach 'Arts-Full Strategies for Public Policy' and lead tours connecting American history, social justice, and artistic engagement. The free exhibition runs through February 14, 2027.

stories.summary: The University of Michigan Museum of Art (UMMA) opened 'We Hold These Truths,' an exhibition by artist Holly Bass, exploring American history and democracy through interactive installations representing 1876, 1976, and 2026. The exhibit features historical settings like an 1876 parlor and 1976 living room, with interactive elements encouraging visitor engagement. Bass emphasized education and community dialogue, while attendees highlighted the importance of connecting students with UMMA's cultural offerings.

stories.title: ArtPrize addresses voting integrity, AI use amid online scrutiny
stories.summary: ArtPrize has issued a statement clarifying its partnership with FlockX, a local marketing tech startup, to ensure voting integrity and data privacy amid online claims about its collaboration with a license plate reader company. The organization also addressed misinformation about AI use in the competition, stating that AI is only permitted as a tool in the New Media category and not as the sole creator of artworks. ArtPrize plans to reevaluate its guidelines in the upcoming off-season with input from artists.

stories.title: As anti-trans attacks escalate, Michigan-based Stand with Trans empowers by building community
stories.summary: Michigan-based Stand with Trans is celebrating Transgender Empowerment Month with a 'Stronger Together' theme, emphasizing community building for transgender people and allies amid rising anti-trans legislation. The organization's events, which began as a local workshop in 2015, now draw international participants and highlight resistance against political attacks. Governor Gretchen Whitmer officially recognized the initiative in 2025.

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities
stories.summary: Michigan's public universities are facing enrollment declines, leading to potential job losses and economic impacts on communities. With state funding stagnant and tuition pressures, universities are struggling to maintain operations, according to the Michigan Association of State Universities. The situation could result in significant job cuts and reduced economic activity across the state.

photo.alt: Daniel Hurley headshot

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities
stories.summary: Michigan's public universities face enrollment declines and limited state funding, leading to potential job losses and economic impacts on communities. With shrinking student numbers and stagnant state aid, regional universities are struggling to maintain operations, affecting local economies through reduced employment and spending.

stories.title: As James pushes local control on data centers, past congressional votes sought to limit just that

stories.title: As Michigan reading scores fall, state superintendent says: ‘We need to improve.’
stories.summary: Michigan's latest state test scores show declining reading proficiency, with political candidates Jocelyn Benson and John James blaming each other for the 'broken' education system. New literacy laws, including mandatory science of reading training for teachers and dyslexia screening, are set to take effect by 2027-2028. State officials emphasize the need for collaboration between lawmakers, educators, and the State Board of Education to improve outcomes, while cautioning that test scores alone do not fully reflect student reading abilities.

stories.title: As Michigan reading scores fall, state superintendent says: ‘We need to improve.’
stories.summary: Michigan's testing structure requires third through seventh graders to take English language arts and math tests, with additional science and social studies exams for fifth and eighth graders. Older students take PSAT and SAT variations, while some students with disabilities take MI-Access tests instead.

stories.title: Auchter's Art: Senate candidates
stories.summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers in distancing themselves from controversial associations. El-Sayed's past connection to streamer Hasan Piker, known for anti-Israel rhetoric, and Rogers' association with Donald Trump are highlighted. stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit revealed that $59 million of Michigan's workforce training funds were used for employer on-the-job training reimbursements instead of education to boost worker skills. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax oversight and documentation, with the state contesting the findings. The report highlights misaligned spending against program goals and calls for improved compliance.

photo.alt: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit found that one-third of $182.5 million in Michigan's Going Pro Talent Fund was spent on new hire orientation instead of education to boost worker skills and wages. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax documentation and oversight, while the state disputed the findings, defending on-the-job training as a valid upskilling method. The 2027 budget for the program is $14.4 million, a 40% decline from the previous year.

The one-bedroom units, including four accessible to people with disabilities, are designated for low-income residents, with eight units for homeless individuals or those earning 30% of the Area Median Income. Competing insurers have exited the Michigan market due to Blue Cross's dominance, forcing residents to seek new coverage.

stories.summary: The Michigan Attorney General must maintain a cooperative agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services for federal IV-D funding to support child support enforcement activities. stories.title: Children found safe in Ohio cornfield after being abducted from Inkster; father found dead at scene
stories.summary: Two boys, ages 6 and 4, were found safe in a cornfield near Norwalk, Ohio, after being allegedly abducted by their father, Brandon Deandre Lee, 36, during a domestic violence incident in Inkster, Michigan. Lee was found dead at the scene after reportedly threatening to kill himself and the children. The mother sustained minor injuries and coordinated with police to locate the children, who were later returned to Michigan with assistance from multiple agencies.

stories.title: Citizens-only voting petition sponsors look to 2028 after initiative fails before state canvassers
stories.summary: Sponsors of a Michigan ballot initiative to implement citizen-only voting and voter ID requirements failed to qualify the measure for the 2026 ballot due to insufficient valid signatures. After losing appeals in both the U.S. and Michigan Supreme Courts, organizers plan to resubmit the petition in 2028 with improved signature collection. Election officials and legal experts dismissed claims of procedural bias, emphasizing the initiative fell short of required validity thresholds.

stories.title: Citizens Research Council outlines impacts of Mop Up Michigan initiative
stories.summary: The Mop Up Michigan Initiative (Proposal 2) seeks to ban political contributions from government contractors, regulated utilities, and related entities to state and local candidates. The Citizens Research Council of Michigan released a report analyzing the proposal's potential impacts, including increased transparency, legal challenges under the First Amendment, and possible effects on contractor participation and utility spending. The initiative faces constitutional questions about the scope of its restrictions and the justification for targeting specific industries.

photo.alt: DTE Energy Headquarters in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Jon King/Michigan Advance)

stories.title: Citizens Research Council outlines impacts of Mop Up Michigan initiative
stories.summary: The Citizens Research Council of Michigan released a report analyzing Proposal 2 (Mop Up Michigan Initiative), which seeks to ban political contributions from government contractors and regulated utilities. The proposal includes enhanced disclosure requirements for political ads and faces potential legal challenges over free speech concerns. While it could increase transparency, implementation may deter contractors from government work and require significant enforcement resources.

stories.title: City Commissions Passes Three Proposals at September Meeting
stories.summary: The City Commission approved three proposals on September 8, 2026, including a multi-modal pathway along Wilcox Road, a new sewer truck for municipal services, and a zoning amendment for multi-family residences. The pathway aims to improve safety for pedestrians and cyclists, while the equipment will enhance maintenance operations. The zoning changes will refine density calculations for multi-family housing.

stories.summary: The Ann Arbor City Council approved a Tenants Bill of Rights and addressed transit safety concerns following a non-lethal car accident on Sept. 10. Over 25 community members rallied for safer infrastructure, with residents highlighting issues like dangerous bike lanes and lack of transparency in road safety progress. The council also discussed deer management and allocated funds from the Kline’s Lot sale to affordable housing and sustainability projects.

stories.title: City Council opposes Proposal E, directs city attorney to challenge in court
stories.summary: Ann Arbor City Council voted 10-1 to direct the city attorney to challenge the legality of Proposal E, a November ballot initiative to replace DTE Energy’s electrical utility with a city-run power grid. The council cited concerns over financial costs and conflicts with the City Charter, which grants utility board creation authority to City Council rather than ballot initiatives. Grassroots group Ann Arbor for Public Power gathered over 5,000 signatures to place the proposal on the ballot, with supporters arguing it aligns with climate goals and energy democracy.

photo.alt: Mayor Christopher Taylor speaks at the City Council meeting at Larcom City Hall Monday evening. Soyeon Kim/DAILY.

stories.title: City Council opposes Proposal E, directs city attorney to challenge in court
stories.summary: Ann Arbor City Council voted 10-1 to direct the city attorney to challenge the legality of Proposal E, a ballot initiative to replace DTE Energy with a city-run power grid. The council cited concerns over financial costs and conflicts with the City Charter, which grants utility board creation authority to the council, not citizens. Grassroots group Ann Arbor for Public Power gathered over 5,000 signatures to place the proposal on the November ballot. Critics argue the council's decision undermines democratic processes, while supporters of the council's stance claim it protects taxpayers and aligns with existing renewable energy initiatives like the Ann Arbor Sustainable Energy Utility (A2SEU).

A resolution directs the City Administrator to develop recommendations for a deer management program, referencing a controversial culling effort from years ago. stories.title: Community
stories.summary: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free. At Greendale Community College, all are accepted and all have a bright future ahead of them. Have you ever felt nervous to deliver a class presentation in front of dozens of strangers? Have you ever been humbled by what you thought would be a blowoff class? Have you ever been helpless to stop petty bickering between close friends? There’s a “Community” episode for each of these issues, and many more. The show captured viewers’ attention with ambitious outings, like “[Modern Warfare](https://youtu.be/XcOG5iZpV-k?si=7RcOVN8nPRSMI8Va)” (a paintball competition set entirely at the college) and “[Remedial Chaos Theory](https://youtu.be/POT3plx0vBs?si=bwUHzhUT4ThVsHjt)” (a timeline-hopping adventure of what-ifs). But in its golden years — specifically Seasons 1-3 — “Community” thrived on its warm relatability and sympathy for a band of misfits [bound together](https://youtu.be/aznTfytzNQ4?si=UXdGH1eh7y_7D85K) by [mutual](https://youtu.be/q44WaM5Rm6A?si=3vzWloDJtpF5duut) [lunacy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dlXuJpuk6oA): the “Study Group.’’ The members of the group are all at different stages of life, but ultimately seeking the same thing: a raw, unadulterated college experience and all the insight it might bring. “Community” is anchored by inventive, witty sitcom writing and a set of comedic powerhouses delivering career-best performances. If you’re in college, there’s never been a better time to watch it.

photo.alt: Courtesy of Ana Torresarpi

stories.title: Detroit cocktail bar goes full horror movie for October
stories.summary: Side Hustle Lounge in downtown Detroit has transformed into the 'Haunted House of Film' for a monthlong Halloween takeover featuring horror movie-themed decor and cocktails. The event includes elaborate scenes inspired by classic horror films and a limited-time menu with drinks like the Bloody Margarita, Purple People Eater, and Trick-or-Treatini, which incorporate themed ingredients and presentation.

photo.alt: Monsters, Inc. cocktail at Side Hustle Lounge

stories.title: Detroit community advocates canvass west side neighborhood after deadly shooting
stories.summary: Community advocates canvassed Detroit’s west-side neighborhood after three people were killed and four injured in an unauthorized after-hours gathering on Prest Street. The effort included city officials, violence intervention groups, and residents addressing concerns about crime, junk cars, and abandoned homes. A public listening session is scheduled for Oct. 5 to gather resident input on needed resources.

photo.alt: Image from the story

stories.title: Detroit community safety official urges man to surrender after mother, daughter shot on city’s east side
stories.summary: A Detroit community safety official urged the man accused of shooting a 29-year-old woman and her 7-year-old daughter to surrender after the incident, which stemmed from a children's dispute. The suspect fled in a white GMC Terrain and is being sought by police. Both victims were hospitalized in stable condition.
entities: Detroit Office of Neighborhood and Community Safety

stories.title: Detroit community violence intervention program shows positive results, study says
stories.summary: A study finds that Detroit's ShotStoppers program, which intervenes in community violence, has led to a decline in gun violence in targeted areas.

stories.title: Detroit council member seeks 18-month pause on data center permits: ‘There are no protections in place’
stories.summary: Detroit Council member Gabriela Santiago-Romero is seeking an 18-month pause on data center permits until formal city regulations are established, citing lack of protections. Her Sept. 29 memorandum requests an interim zoning moratorium to delay permitting for enterprise AI data centers until March 2028. The initiative follows a March council resolution urging a two-year moratorium and ongoing efforts by the City Planning Commission to draft a zoning policy by Dec. 31, 2026.
entities: Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department

stories.title: Detroit Council Member Seeks Moratorium on New Data Center Permits Until March 2028
stories.summary: Detroit Council member Gabriela Santiago-Romero has requested a draft ordinance to temporarily pause new data center permits until March 2028, as the city works on formal zoning regulations. This follows a March 2026 council resolution urging a two-year moratorium, which Mayor Mary Sheffield has not acted on. The City Planning Commission aims to finalize a permanent data center zoning policy by December 31, 2026, but the legal path for Santiago-Romero's proposal remains unclear with most council members supporting the existing zoning amendment process.
entities: Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department

stories.title: Detroit Cultivator Hytek Is Dropping One of the Hottest Weed Strains of 2026
stories.summary: Detroit-based cannabis cultivator Hytek is releasing Toad Venom, a highly sought-after strain with origins in a crossbreed of Animal Face and Sin Mintz genetics. The strain, known for its potency and unique flavor profile, will be available in Michigan on October 16, 2026, at The Refinery in Detroit with competitive pricing. Hytek's version uses the Green Dragon phenotype, which has become a market standout due to its scarcity and high demand.

stories.title: Detroit Democrats challenge Mike Rogers’ touted gains with Black voters in US Senate race
stories.summary: Detroit Democrats and civic leaders criticized Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers for his historical record on Black voter suppression and education policies, challenging his claims of Black voter outreach success. They highlighted his role in legislation that led to state control of Detroit schools, while Rogers' campaign dismissed the criticism as 'fourth quarter theatrics.'

stories.summary: Detroit Disability Power is hiring a visual artist to expand its reach and create accessible graphics for social media, email, print and online spaces. The full-time position pays a salary of $55,000-$62,000 plus benefits. Apply by Sept. 23.

stories.summary: Detroit charter schools show significant performance gaps, with some achieving high proficiency rates while others struggle. stories.title: Detroit ethics board seeks independent counsel for Conrad Mallett probe
stories.summary: The Detroit Board of Ethics is working to secure independent legal counsel to investigate Corporation Counsel Conrad Mallett, who earned $1.8 million from Lear Corp. while approving a $4 million tax break for the company. A three-member panel will select an attorney for the investigation.

photo.alt: Detroit ethics board seeks independent counsel for Conrad Mallett probe

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: $2.7M contract approved for lights and surveillance at four parks in the city
stories.summary: The city of Detroit approved a three-year, $2.7 million contract for surveillance cameras and lighting in four parks across the city. Detroit-based Bayview Electric Company will provide the service for public walkways in Chandler Park, Eliza-Howell Park, Maheras Gentry Park and Rouge Park. The contract comes after residents have voiced concerns over privacy and surveillance from third party companies, most recently Flock cameras and ShotSpotter.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: $2.7M contract approved for lights and surveillance at four parks in the city

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: City council to look into poor conditions at the Greenhouse Apartments
stories.summary: Detroit City Council is investigating reports of poor conditions at the Greenhouse Apartments, a subsidized senior housing facility on Detroit's west side. Tenants allege issues including bedbugs, non-working elevators, and inhumane living conditions. Council President Pro Tempore Coleman A Young II raised the concerns during a formal session, prompting multiple city departments to assess the situation and consider penalties against building managers.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: City council to look into poor conditions at the Greenhouse Apartments

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Comerica Park receives a new name
stories.summary: Comerica Park, home of the Detroit Tigers, will be renamed Fifth Third Park after Fifth Third Bancorp acquired Comerica Bank. The name change, effective next year, follows the bank's rebranding of all branch locations. Michigan Regional President Steve Davis emphasized the significance of the park to Detroit's community pride.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: Comerica Park receives a new name

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Companies give seniors produce boxes to promote brain health on Alzheimer’s Day
stories.summary: Eli Lilly and Company and Planet Harvest are distributing over 1,300 brain-healthy produce boxes to food-insecure seniors in Metro Detroit on World Alzheimer’s Day. The boxes include apples, cabbage, cucumbers, collard greens, lemons, oranges, corn, and zucchinis. Seniors can pick up boxes at locations like Rochester Christian University and Webster Community Center, with door-to-door distributions at senior living homes.

photo.alt: Seniors receiving produce boxes to support brain health

stories.summary: The Detroit People’s Food Co-op is seeking more residents to buy into the neighborhood grocery store. The co-op is running...

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: First 13 winners of Make Detroit Home grant announced
stories.summary: The citywide coalition MoveDetroit is announcing the first 13 winners of a grant aimed at increasing and stabilizing the city’s population. The initial Make Detroit Home awards are worth $15,000 each. One of the recipients is local entrepreneur Karissma Yve, who plans to use the funds to scale her business and invest in community hiring.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: First 13 winners of Make Detroit Home grant announced

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Kamala Harris endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit
stories.summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris endorsed Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate at an event in Detroit. She highlighted his potential as a national voice for the state. El-Sayed addressed concerns from Arab and Muslim voters who previously supported Trump or minor candidates due to Biden administration policies on Israel.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: Kamala Harris endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: MDHHS to award $1.5 million for community violence intervention initiatives
stories.summary: Five organizations, including two in Detroit, will receive $1.5 million in funding from the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) for community violence intervention programs. The grants aim to reduce firearm violence and its impacts in historically disinvested neighborhoods through public health and safety initiatives. Each recipient will receive $300,000 for a two-year project running from September 1, 2026, to September 30, 2028.

photo.alt: Detroit's skyline from Belle Isle on November 16, 2023

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Nonprofit LGBT Detroit provides mental health services at new facility on the city’s West side
stories.summary: LGBT Detroit Health, a nonprofit, is opening a new wellness center on Detroit's West side offering mental health services, fitness classes, and chronic care management. The facility provides a safe space for the LGBT community and partners with local health organizations for testing and vaccinations. It is funded through state grants and membership fees.

photo.alt: Image from WDET 101.9 FM

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: ShotStoppers program significantly decreased gun violence, says University of Michigan report
stories.summary: A University of Michigan analysis found a 45% decrease in homicides and nonfatal shootings in Detroit since the launch of the ShotStoppers community violence intervention program three years ago. The program funds community-based organizations with $175,000 per quarter and performance-based bonuses to reduce gun violence in high-risk areas.

photo.alt: Image from WDET 101.9 FM

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Statue of former Detroit Mayor Coleman A. Young to be instated at U.S. Capitol
stories.summary: The Coleman A Young Foundation’s years-long efforts to install a statue of former Detroit mayor Coleman A. Young in the U.S. Capitol are nearing completion, funded by entities like the DTE Foundation, Bedrock, The Ilitch family, and individuals John A. James and Suzanne Shank. The statue will replace a marble sculpture of Lewis Cass, a former Michigan governor who supported slavery, and will be displayed in the Capitol’s National Statutory Hall Collection. An event celebrating the announcement will be hosted by the Charles H. Wright Museum on October 20.

photo.alt: Coleman A Young Municipal Center pictured Aug. 8, 2017

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report will be back in the new year
stories.summary: The Detroit Evening Report is taking a hiatus until January 2027. The program plans to return with new content in the new year and is encouraging listeners to support its continuation.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report will be back in the new year

stories.title: Detroit expands efforts to curb chronic absenteeism with free bus service and new programs
stories.summary: Detroit is continuing free bus service for all students and launching a rideshare program at four high schools to reduce chronic absenteeism. The district is also expanding a program that rewards high school and middle school students for perfect attendance and increasing yellow school bus service at high-absenteeism schools.

photo.alt: Detroit expands efforts to curb chronic absenteeism with free bus service and new programs

stories.title: Detroit explores alternatives to DTE Energy monopoly
stories.summary: Detroit City Council and Mayor Mary Sheffield's administration are investigating alternatives to DTE Energy's near-monopoly as the city's energy provider. Council members criticized frequent power outages and rate hikes, requesting a report on how other municipalities have diversified energy sources.

photo.alt: Detroit explores alternatives to DTE Energy monopoly

stories.title: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing
stories.summary: The family of Kimberlly Moore claims her body was accidentally cremated before her scheduled viewing at Hutchison Funeral Home, leading to a demand for answers. The funeral home has launched an internal investigation and stated they will address the issue if found at fault.

photo.alt: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing

stories.title: Detroit Farm and Cider owner sells property after legal disputes
stories.summary: Leandra King, owner of Detroit Farm and Cider, is selling her property for $5.3 million after years of legal disputes with the city over animal possession and code violations. The city recently seized animals from the property.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Detroit Fire Battalion Chief charged after alleged road rage attack in Livonia
stories.summary: A Detroit Fire Department Battalion Chief, Thomas Suchora, was charged with assault and malicious destruction of property after allegedly attacking 64-year-old Todd Richards during a road rage incident in Livonia on Aug. 25. Suchora, who has been with the department since 1995, was placed on unpaid leave following the Sept. 9 criminal charges and is scheduled for a preliminary hearing on Oct. 8. Richards, who has a pacemaker and is awaiting a kidney transplant, plans to file a civil lawsuit over the destruction of his $1,200 phone and injuries sustained.

photo.alt: Detroit Fire Battalion Chief charged after alleged road rage attack in Livonia

stories.title: Detroit Forecast: Cool temps, rain chance ahead
stories.summary: Southeast Michigan will experience cooler-than-normal temperatures through mid-week with a slight chance of light showers Wednesday. High pressure will keep conditions dry through the weekend before warming into the lower 70s. The next significant rain is expected no earlier than mid-next week.

stories.summary: The Detroit Free Press has published a 2026 general election voter guide featuring candidates in Wayne, Oakland, Macomb counties and some statewide races. stories.summary: The Detroit Harvest Fest in October 2026 and the Movies in the Park program featured Metroparks' pop-up educational activities tied to movie themes. stories.summary: A health fair in Detroit offered free health screenings, groceries, and resources to families. Forgotten Harvest provided fresh groceries, emphasizing nutrition's role in health. Lisa Williams, executive director of New Beginnings CDC, highlighted the event's positive impact on the community.

photo.alt: Detroit health fair brings free screenings, groceries, resources to families

stories.title: Detroit high school assistant football coach accused of shooting and injuring mother, 7-year-old
stories.summary: A Detroit high school assistant football coach, Aaron Matthew Wright, faces 17 charges after allegedly shooting and injuring a woman and her 7-year-old daughter during an argument over a fight between children. The incident occurred on October 12, and Wright was arrested the next day. The victims were hospitalized but are expected to recover.

photo.alt: Aaron Matthew Wright (Wayne County Prosecutor's Office)

stories.summary: Detroit is Unrivaled presented by Ally is set for September 14, 2026. The event is part of a series of announcements from 313 Presents, including Trans-Siberian Orchestra's 30th Anniversary Winter Tour on December 23, 2026.

stories.title: Detroit legend Olayami Dabls brings his artistry to Ann Arbor
stories.summary: Detroit artist Olayami Dabls, known for his work at the MBAD African Bead Museum and Dabls African Bead Gallery, is participating in a residency at the University of Michigan Institute for the Humanities. The Institute's gallery is hosting 'Grand Vision,' an exhibition featuring his paintings, African Trade Beads, and N'kisi figures. His iconic sculpture 'Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners' has been temporarily relocated to the U-M campus through October 11.
entities: University of Michigan Institute for the Humanities

photo.alt: An outdoor art installation featuring a table and chairs.

stories.title: Detroit legend Olayami Dabls brings his artistry to Ann Arbor
stories.summary: Detroit artist Olayami Dabls is showcasing his work through a residency at the University of Michigan Institute for the Humanities, featuring an exhibition titled 'Grand Vision' and the temporary relocation of his sculpture 'Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners' to the U-M campus through October 11. The exhibit includes paintings, African Trade Beads, and a recreation of Dabls' office, with public workshops planned for October 13.
entities: University of Michigan Institute for the Humanities

stories.title: Detroit Lions Day at the Zoo features Roary the mascot
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions will host a special event at the Detroit Zoo on September 20, 2026, with their mascot Roary meeting fans. The event is part of the Lions' community outreach initiatives.

photo.alt: Roary the Detroit Lions mascot will be on hand during the Detroit Lions Day at the Zoo, Sat. Sept. 20, 2026 to meet fans. (Photo courtesy of the Detroit Zoo Facebook page)

stories.title: Detroit Lions’ Jameson Williams won’t face charges following alleged domestic violence investigation
stories.summary: The Oakland County Prosecutor’s Office announced it will not file charges against Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams after investigating an alleged domestic violence incident that occurred on August 6 and was reported to Novi police in September. Investigators reviewed evidence including statements, photos, and communications, but concluded there was no cause for charges. Williams’ attorneys denied the allegations, stating the claims are baseless.

photo.alt: Jameson Williams of the Detroit Lions during an NFL game on September 13, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan.

stories.title: Detroit man arrested in August shooting at Oakland County park
stories.summary: A Detroit man has been arrested more than a month after he allegedly shot a man at a park in Oakland County. Ruben Aleman Contreras faces six felony charges, including assault with intent to murder and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. The incident occurred on August 23 at Jaycee Park in Pontiac, leaving the victim with gunshot wounds to the abdomen and right buttock.

photo.alt: Decal on side of shiny black police vehicle

stories.title: Detroit man charged with murder after deadly Warren flea market refund dispute
stories.summary: A 41-year-old Detroit man, Zarick Lamont Johnson, was arraigned on a first-degree murder charge following a dispute at the County Line Flea Market in Warren. Prosecutors allege Johnson assaulted a man and then drove his van into his brother, killing him. Johnson faces charges including first-degree murder and felony offenses involving a motor vehicle.

photo.alt: Detroit man charged with murder after deadly Warren flea market refund dispute

stories.title: Detroit man charged with murder in ‘random’ stabbing of Chipotle worker
stories.summary: A 42-year-old Detroit man, Devon Jason Watson, has been charged with first-degree murder in the fatal stabbing of 34-year-old Chipotle employee Jaquoya Wix. Prosecutors described the attack as random but premeditated. Watson and Wix did not know each other, and the stabbing occurred in an alley behind a downtown Detroit restaurant on Sept. 20, 2026.

photo.alt: Gavel MLive (File photo | MLive.com)

stories.title: Detroit man charged with threatening Mayor Mary Sheffield, given $50K bond
stories.summary: A 55-year-old Detroit man was charged with making a terrorist threat after allegedly threatening to harm Mayor Mary Sheffield and shoot up a downtown government building. Sterling Anthony Peters was given a $50,000 bond and ordered to remain under house arrest following his arraignment on Oct. 8, 2026. The incidents occurred on Oct. 5 at two Detroit government buildings, with prosecutors describing the threats as 'very disturbing' and a growing concern for public officials.

photo.alt: Mary Sheffield

stories.title: Detroit man shot neighbor during argument over trash can, feds say
stories.summary: Federal authorities accuse Counsel Gaynor, a convicted felon, of shooting his Detroit neighbor during a trash can dispute on Sept. 9, 2024. Gaynor, who has prior felony convictions including armed robbery and firearm possession, allegedly discarded the weapon after the incident. A federal charge of firearm possession by a felon was filed after earlier state charges were dismissed due to the victim's absence as a witness.
entities: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives

photo.alt: Detroit man shot neighbor during argument over trash can, feds say

stories.title: Detroit man threatens Mayor Sheffield, Wayne County Prosecutor fires back
stories.summary: A Detroit man was arrested for threatening Mayor Mary Sheffield on October 5, 2026. Sterling Anthony Peters made two threats—first at the Coleman A. Young Municipal Center and later at Detroit Police Headquarters—before being charged with making a false report or threat of terrorism. Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy condemned the threats, vowing to prosecute the case 'beyond a reasonable doubt.' Peters was arraigned on October 8, 2026, with a $50,000 bond and placed on house arrest.

photo.alt: Detroit man threatens Mayor Sheffield, Wayne County Prosecutor fires back

stories.title: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield declines comment on OIG investigation into Bettison call with activist
stories.summary: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield declined to comment on an Office of Inspector General investigation into a recorded call between Police Chief Todd Bettison and activist Jahdante Smith. The call, recorded in August, involved Bettison asking Smith to remove social media posts featuring old photos of Sheffield. Sheffield stated the matter is under investigation and urged allowing the process to proceed without comment.

photo.alt: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield declines comment on OIG investigation into Bettison call with activist

stories.title: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield offers support to family of teen killed in drive-by shooting
stories.summary: A 16-year-old girl was killed in a drive-by shooting on Detroit’s east side, with another person wounded. Mayor Mary Sheffield condemned the violence and urged residents to provide information. Detroit homicide detectives are investigating the incident.

photo.alt: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield offers support to family of teen killed in drive-by shooting

stories.summary: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield addresses a controversial call she received.

stories.title: Detroit media exec was accused of posting racist meme. Now he owes $62M in discrimination case.
stories.summary: A federal jury ordered Detroit media executive Kevin Adell and The Word Network to pay Bishop George Bloomer $62.2 million in a discrimination case. The lawsuit alleged Adell created a racially hostile work environment by sharing a racist meme depicting Bloomer and other Black clergy members, leading to Bloomer's 2019 departure. Adell's spokesperson declined to comment after the verdict.

source.name: Jenny Sherman, Khalil Maycock, Joel Deaner

photo.alt: Detroit media exec was accused of posting racist meme. Now he owes $62M in discrimination case.

stories.title: Detroit men charged in Southfield ‘revenge’ shooting that killed dog
stories.summary: Two Detroit men were charged in a Southfield shooting that police believe was a misguided act of revenge. The incident occurred on September 28, 2026, when a man fired nine rounds into a home, injuring the homeowner's pit bull, Kane, who had to be euthanized. DeMarco Lewis confessed to the shooting, claiming he believed the homeowner's son had stolen his car, though no evidence of a theft was found.

photo.alt: Detroit men charged in Southfield ‘revenge’ shooting that killed dog

stories.title: Detroit Month of Design offers community engagement opportunities
stories.summary: Detroit Month of Design provides residents with opportunities to shape the city’s future through events and projects. The newsletter highlights ways to get involved in urban design and community development.

photo.alt: “Detroit Public Library, 1865, 1963” in golden letters is engraved in a granite façade of a white stone building with four red pillars.

stories.title: Detroit opens new round of home repair grants
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Detroit homes need repairs, with a cost estimate of over $1 billion. The city has launched a new round of grants through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs, expected to repair around 250 homes. Applications are online-only, creating barriers for residents without internet access.

photo.alt: Ceiling with plaster and drywall damage exposes wooden joists and lath.

stories.title: Detroit parents, community members want change
stories.summary: Detroit parents and community members are calling for a new school board to challenge the status quo, with some advocating for faster progress, increased accountability, and expanded measures of student success beyond graduation rates. Stakeholders like Jasmine Johnson, Gwen Moore, and Cyekeia Lee emphasize the need for collaboration between schools and families to improve educational outcomes.

photo.alt: Detroit parents, community members want change

stories.title: Detroit People’s Food Co-op asks for more support to stay open
stories.summary: The Detroit People’s Food Co-op is seeking more residents to buy into the neighborhood grocery store as it runs out of money. They launched a campaign for 500 new owners and ask customers to spend $10 when they come in. The co-op opened in 2024 to address the lack of Black-owned grocery stores in Detroit, aiming for community ownership of the food system rather than just shopping there. However, the store's affordability remains a challenge given that 34% of Detroiters live in poverty, despite generating nearly $3 million annually.

photo.alt: Detroit People's Food Co-op exterior

stories.title: Detroit Pistons star Cade Cunningham to meet fans at free Xfinity event in Bloomfield Hills
stories.summary: Detroit Pistons star Cade Cunningham will meet fans during a free basketball-themed event at the Xfinity store in Bloomfield Hills on October 17, 2026. The event features interactive experiences, giveaways, and appearances by the Pistons Drumline, Pistons Dancers, and Hooper. Cunningham’s meet-and-greet is scheduled from 3 to 4 p.m., with DJ Myint performing starting at 1:30 p.m.

photo.alt: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons interacts with fans after a game at Little Caesars Arena

stories.title: Detroit police asking public for help finding missing 28-year-old man
stories.summary: Detroit police are asking the public for help in locating a missing 28-year-old man.

stories.title: Detroit Police Commissioner rescinds virtual public comment ban
stories.summary: Detroit Police Commissioner Henrietta Ivey rescinded her motion to ban virtual public comments at Board of Police Commissioners meetings following public outcry. The board shortened public comment time to 90 seconds and prioritized accessibility for people with disabilities.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Detroit police want help finding missing 51-year-old man
stories.summary: Police are seeking information about Timothy King, a 51-year-old man who went missing in Detroit on Sept. 15, 2026. He was last seen near Evergreen Road and Fenkell Avenue wearing a white T-shirt, black shorts, and gray tennis shoes. Authorities are asking the public for assistance in locating him.

photo.alt: Detroit Police Department missing person alert for Timothy King

stories.title: Detroit probes side hustle: Ethics investigation into Corporation Counsel
stories.summary: The Detroit Board of Ethics is seeking independent legal counsel to investigate Corporation Counsel Conrad Mallett, who earned $1.8 million from Lear Corp. while approving a $4 million tax break for the company.

photo.alt: Image related to the Gordie Howe Bridge and Detroit home repair initiatives.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools and DFT Reach Tentative Agreement on Class Size Overage Pay for 2026-2028
stories.summary: A tentative agreement between Detroit Public Schools Community District and the Detroit Federation of Teachers outlines new class size overage compensation for the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 school years. The agreement replaces existing formulas with specific class size targets, including thresholds for K-3, 4-5, 6-12, and special education classifications, and expires on June 30, 2028.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools and DFT Tentative Agreement Expires in 2028
stories.summary: A tentative agreement between Detroit Public Schools Community District and the Detroit Federation of Teachers (DFT) outlines terms for occupational therapists' caseloads, overage supplemental payments, and a June 30, 2028 expiration date. The agreement specifies quarterly payments for overage supplements, with the final payment due by the second July paycheck. Provisions of the existing DFT collective bargaining agreement remain in effect beyond this letter.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools Tentative Agreement 2026-2028: Teacher Payments for Oversized Classes
stories.summary: The tentative agreement outlines payment structures for teachers in Detroit Public Schools when class sizes exceed contractual maximums. Payments vary based on the number of students above the limit, with amounts per quarter and annual totals specified. Conditions include mutual acknowledgment of oversized classes and efforts to reduce enrollments.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools to Allow PD Days for Bilingual Education
stories.summary: The tentative agreement allows teachers to use one of three designated Professional Development Days for training specific to the Office of Bilingual Education and Related Programs, as determined by the District’s Office of Curriculum and Instruction.

stories.title: Detroit reports 101 properties damaged after EF-2 tornado
stories.summary: Detroit’s storm response update shows 101 properties damaged by the Sept. 3 EF-2 tornado — the city’s first since 1997 — with the hardest-hit areas including McDougall-Hunt, Islandview, West Village, Indian Village, East Village, Pingree Park and Belle Isle. Mayor Mary Sheffield declared a local state of emergency. Crews removed 295 fallen trees, cleared 83 streets, hauled 342 tons of debris, and restored power to all traffic signals, though full recovery is expected to take time.

photo.alt: Detroit reports 101 properties damaged after EF-2 tornado

stories.title: 🗑️ Detroit’s ‘bottom of the barrel’ voting machines
stories.summary: Voters with disabilities were not buying what the city clerk was selling at the Oct. 12 Election Commission meeting.

photo.alt: 🗑️ Detroit’s ‘bottom of the barrel’ voting machines

stories.title: Detroit's Corktown to host Michigan space hub. What we know
stories.summary: Michigan officials announced a new 'space hub' in Detroit's Corktown neighborhood, supported by a $1.2 million grant from the Michigan Office of Defense and Aerospace Innovation. The hub, located at Newlab within the Michigan Central Innovation District, will launch on October 28, 2026. It aims to accelerate growth in Michigan’s space economy by connecting manufacturers, startups, and researchers.
entities: Michigan Office of Defense and Aerospace Innovation (ODAI)

photo.alt: Aerial view of Michigan Central Innovation District or related development area

stories.title: Detroit’s feeling spooky: Celebrate Halloween, Harvest Fest and more
stories.summary: Detroiters can enjoy Halloween parties, harvest festivals, and campfires this October. The article provides a list of fall activities and events.

photo.alt: A brown dog with a sheet covering its face is dressed like a ghost.

stories.title: Detroit’s Greektown looks different after $20M makeover. Here’s what’s new
stories.summary: A $20 million transformation of Detroit’s historic Greektown neighborhood is complete, featuring wider sidewalks, expanded outdoor dining, and smart street technology. The Monroe Streetscape Project includes pedestrian-friendly upgrades, a 10-gigabit internet backbone, and 124 HD cameras integrated with the Detroit Police Department’s Real-Time Crime Center. City and state leaders celebrated the project’s completion with a Greek cultural ceremony on Oct. 14, 2026.

photo.alt: Greektown streetscape with wider sidewalks and outdoor dining areas

stories.title: Detroit's Home Repair Crisis: A New Round of Grants
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of homes in Detroit urgently need repairs, with a cost estimated at over $1 billion. The city has opened a new round of grants through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs, expected to repair around 250 homes. However, the online-only preapplication poses a barrier for residents without internet access.

photo.alt: Ceiling with plaster and drywall damage exposes wooden joists and lath.

stories.title: Detroit's New Home Repair Grants Aim to Address $1 Billion Problem
stories.summary: Detroit has opened a new round of grants to repair homes, targeting around 250 properties through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs. The preapplication process is online, creating barriers for residents without internet access, though a helpline is available for assistance. The city acknowledges the need for a more accessible system.

photo.alt: Detroit's New Home Repair Grants Aim to Address $1 Billion Problem

stories.title: Detroit’s new in-person entry point for shelter system
stories.summary: The Detroit Continuum of Care (CoC) Board of Directors announced a new in-person access point for Detroit’s shelter system at the Northwest Activities Center, staffed by Wayne Metropolitan Community Action Agency. The lease with Cass Community Social Services will not be renewed after October 31. Board members also expressed support for more in-person hearings to improve accountability.
entities: Detroit Continuum of Care (CoC) Board of Directors

photo.alt: Detroit’s new in-person entry point for shelter system

stories.title: Detroit’s reading growth outpaces similar districts
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) students showed more growth in K-2 reading scores between 2022-23 and 2025-26 compared to 12 unnamed similar districts, despite having a lower percentage of students on grade level (27.2% vs. 31.4%). The district is using funds from a 2016 federal 'right to read' civil rights lawsuit to improve early literacy through initiatives like hiring interventionists, reducing class sizes, and offering merit pay for educators meeting literacy goals. Board members emphasize the urgency of continued progress as the settlement money runs out.

photo.alt: Detroit’s reading growth outpaces similar districts

stories.title: Detroit school board appoints 25-year-old youth advocate as its newest member
stories.summary: Jeremiah Steen, a 25-year-old philanthropist and youth advocate, was appointed to the Detroit Public Schools Community District board to fill a vacancy left by the death of member Iris Taylor. Steen will serve through December 2026 and aims to focus on workforce development and student economic mobility. The appointment followed a competitive selection process with third-party evaluation.

photo.alt: Jeremiah Steen answers the board's questions in an interview for the position

stories.title: Detroit school board appoints 25-year-old youth advocate to fill open seat
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District has appointed a 25-year-old youth advocate to fill an open school board seat. Steen, a University of Detroit Jesuit and University of Detroit Mercy graduate, previously ran for the board in 2024 but placed 16th out of 22 candidates. He currently serves as a community growth fellow at a Michigan nonprofit and was a former trustee of the Skillman Foundation, a Chalkbeat funder.
entities: University of Detroit Jesuit High School and Academy
Community Economic Development Association of Michigan

stories.title: Detroit School board candidates and voter awareness
stories.summary: Citizen Detroit is encouraging its audience to share candidate interviews for the 25 Detroit School Board candidates running in the November 3 election. The interviews cover candidates' priorities for students and their goals for the board.

photo.alt: Detroit School board candidates and voter awareness

stories.title: Detroit School Board Election Features 34 Candidates for 5 Seats
stories.summary: The Detroit Public School Community District school board election will see 34 candidates competing for five open seats. Only 19 of the 34 candidates responded to Chalkbeat Detroit's outreach about their priorities and views on district challenges. Voters will choose among them on November 3.

photo.alt: Detroit School Board Election Features 34 Candidates for 5 Seats

stories.title: Detroit school board must fill open seat ahead of November election
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) school board must fill an open seat before the November election. Brenda Butler, a former City Year Detroit leader and fourth-highest vote-getter in the 2024 election, is a potential candidate but has not confirmed her interest. The dates for upcoming interviews have not yet been publicly posted.

photo.alt: Detroit school board must fill open seat ahead of November election

stories.title: Detroit school board reconsiders plans to demolish four closed buildings
stories.summary: The Detroit school board is reconsidering plans to demolish four closed buildings, which would cost nearly $5 million according to a district report. Board member Ida Simmons-Short suggested prioritizing classroom resources over demolition costs and proposed selling the buildings to generate more funds for students. Thurgood Marshall Elementary-Middle School is next on the district’s list of small schools to close in 2027, with 17 more buildings under review for high operating costs due to low enrollment.

photo.alt: Detroit school board reconsiders plans to demolish four closed buildings

stories.title: Detroit school board’s chair and vice chair will not seek reelection in November
stories.summary: Two Detroit school board leaders, LaTrice McClendon and Corletta Vaughn, will not seek reelection in November, citing personal reasons and disqualification due to late fees. Their departure may lead to a significant shift in the district's governance and policies.

photo.alt: DPSCD board chair LaTrice McClendon, left, and vice chair Corletta Vaughn, are not running for reelection. They are shown in a June 2025 meeting reading a statement about a district student who had been detained by federal immigration officials. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school board signals desire to find alternatives to demolition for four closed buildings
stories.summary: The Detroit school board is reconsidering plans to demolish four recently closed schools after community criticism. Originally scheduled for demolition in June 2027, the board is exploring alternatives like selling or leasing the buildings. The four schools closed due to low enrollment and high costs, with demolition estimated to cost nearly $5 million.

photo.alt: Some board members for the Detroit Public Schools Community District are reconsidering plans to demolish four school buildings that closed at the end of the 2025-26 school year. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school board to fill vacant seat of late member Iris Taylor ahead of November election
stories.summary: The Detroit school board must appoint a new member to fill the vacant seat left by late board member Iris Taylor before the November election. The board plans to interview candidates, including the 2024 election runner-up Sherisse Butler, with a third-party law firm tallying scores to determine the appointment. The selected candidate will serve through the end of 2026.

photo.alt: The DPSCD board must fill an open seat before the November election. Pictured, board members meet to interview candidates in July 2025. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy requiring documentation for early student pickups, limiting them to 'rare occurrences' and prohibiting unexcused departures in the final 30 minutes of the school day. Parents will face mandatory meetings and attendance contracts if their children accumulate multiple unexcused early sign-outs, with consequences including chronic absenteeism tracking and grade retention for affected students.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit school district has adopted a new policy to address unexcused early sign-outs, with parents expressing mixed reactions. While some support protecting instructional time, others raise concerns about socioeconomic barriers and the needs of students with disabilities. The district acknowledges limited research on partial-day absenteeism and its impact on learning.

Parents expressed mixed reactions, with some supporting the change to protect instructional time and others raising concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. The district highlights the issue similarly to its efforts against chronic absenteeism, though limited research exists on effective solutions for partial-day absences.

stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy to address partial-day absenteeism by curbing unexcused early sign-outs. Parents and caregivers expressed mixed reactions, with some supporting the change to protect instructional time and others raising concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. The district highlights the issue alongside efforts to reduce chronic absenteeism, citing limited research on effective solutions for partial-day absences.

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy to address partial-day absenteeism, where students leave school early without excused reasons. Parents expressed mixed reactions, with some supporting the policy to protect instructional time and others raising concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. Limited research exists on solutions for partial-day absenteeism, though studies suggest more instructional time improves academic performance. DPSCD has previously made progress reducing chronic absenteeism through parent education efforts.

stories.title: Detroit school district and some charters lag behind state
stories.summary: In spring 2026, Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed long-term growth in M-STEP proficiency rates but lagged behind statewide averages. Many Detroit charter schools also underperformed compared to the state, though some, like Pembroke Academy, outperformed both the district and state averages in multiple subjects.

photo.alt: Detroit school district and some charters lag behind state

stories.title: Detroit school district releases 2026-27 calendar
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District has released its 2026-27 school year calendar, with a start date of Aug. 24 for students. The calendar includes 175 student attendance days and five professional development days for staff, meeting Michigan's 180-day minimum. It does not observe Eid al-Fitr, a Muslim holiday expected on March 10, despite advocacy from students and community members.

photo.alt: Detroit school district releases 2026-27 calendar

stories.title: Detroit school district’s tax proposal gets voter approval
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools' operating millage proposal, which needed voter approval by July 2027, has been approved. The tax applies to commercial, rental, and vacation properties but not primary residences. The approval avoids potential November elections if the proposal had failed.
