stories.title: Detroit Schools Partner with MSU to Expand Autism Teacher Pipeline
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District and Michigan State University are collaborating to expand training for educators supporting students with autism. The partnership aims to equip teachers with specialized knowledge to create effective learning environments. Early detection of autism through district programs allows families to identify special needs before kindergarten, though some parents face barriers to diagnosis.

photo.alt: Detroit Schools Partner with MSU to Expand Autism Teacher Pipeline

stories.title: Detroit students canvass to ask voters to support Proposal S
stories.summary: Detroit students and volunteers with 482Forward are canvassing to promote Proposal S, a school millage on the Aug. 4 primary ballot that would allow Detroit Public Schools Community District to collect its own operating tax. If not approved by July 1, 2027, the district faces an $111 million deficit. The campaign aims to educate voters about the millage, which replaces a previous system and ensures continued funding for schools.

photo.alt: Lindsey Matson, deputy director of youth organizing for 482Forward, explains Proposal S to a voter in Corktown.

stories.title: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator
stories.summary: The Detroit superintendent addressed viral criticisms from a content creator, stating the district intends to respond legally to baseless information. The discussion included procedures for contractor proposals and efforts to replace contractors with full-time staff, particularly in janitorial roles.

photo.alt: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator

stories.title: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) Superintendent Vitti addressed viral social media criticisms and outlined the district's legal response to 'baseless information.' He discussed efforts to reduce reliance on contracted services, including challenges in hiring in-house janitorial staff, and highlighted progress since emergency management ended in 2016. The board is considering increasing in-house custodial staff to improve school cleanliness.

photo.alt: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator

stories.title: Detroit teen accused of threatening sister, stabbing her dog
stories.summary: An 18-year-old Detroit man was charged after allegedly threatening his sister with a pocketknife and stabbing her dog during a domestic dispute. Joshua Shakur Leroy Cawthon faces charges including felonious assault, domestic violence, and first-degree killing/torturing animals. The incident occurred on Oct. 3, and he turned himself in the same day; his court dates are scheduled for October 21 and 28.

photo.alt: Man charged in Wayne County. (File photo | MLive.com) MLive file photo

stories.title: Detroit Tenants Union Lawsuit: Evictions and Compliance
stories.summary: The Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit challenges eviction practices tied to housing compliance, with landlords warning of market collapse due to maintenance costs and tenants arguing safety shouldn't depend on profitability. The next hearing is set for Sept. 21, where a judge may rule on a motion to dismiss the case.

photo.alt: A row of older red-brick-and-wood houses with porches and trees line the street under a gray, overcast sky.

stories.title: Detroit to Host Ninth Annual Halloween in the D 2026 Event
stories.summary: Detroit will host its ninth annual Halloween in the D event from Oct. 24, Oct. 31, and Nov. 7, featuring family-friendly and spooky activities. Last year's event distributed 1 million pieces of candy, raised $104,000 in donations, and attracted 30,000 attendees with 700 volunteers. WDET will provide exclusive podcasts covering the event.

photo.alt: Halloween in the D event promotional image

stories.title: Detroit to Receive $1.25M for Right-to-Counsel Eviction Program
stories.summary: The city of Detroit in Wayne County will receive $1.25 million to implement a right-to-counsel program for tenants facing eviction proceedings. This initiative aims to provide legal support to city tenants during eviction processes.

stories.title: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.
stories.summary: The Avenue of Fashion is highlighted as a test case for expanding retail in Detroit's neighborhoods. Surrounding areas like Sherwood Forest and Palmer Woods contribute to the corridor's potential, with existing businesses such as Bakers Keyboard Lounge adding to its appeal. Strategies include increasing year-round activity through winter events and holiday shopping to boost foot traffic beyond the summer season.

photo.alt: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.

stories.title: Detroit woman accused of accidentally shooting, injuring 13-year-old sister pleads guilty
stories.summary: A 21-year-old Detroit woman, Adriana Arnold, has pleaded guilty to accidentally shooting her 13-year-old sister with an unsecured firearm in the bathroom on August 25, 2026. The incident occurred on Detroit’s west side near Puritan Avenue, and the victim was hospitalized for a gunshot wound to her left arm. Arnold will be sentenced on November 10, 2026.

photo.alt: Detroit woman accused of accidentally shooting, injuring 13-year-old sister pleads guilty

stories.title: Detroit woman facing human trafficking, prostitution charges after victim seeks help from motel housekeeper
stories.summary: A Detroit woman has been charged with operating a human trafficking enterprise in Southfield after an alleged prostitution victim sought help from a motel housekeeper. Prosecutors say the victim was lured into prostitution by Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, and was forced to perform sex acts. The victim approached a housekeeper at the Marvins Garden Inn on Sept. 10, prompting police to be contacted and Robinson to be arrested.

photo.alt: Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, of Detroit, is facing multiple felony charges for allegedly trafficking a woman into prostitution at a Southfield motel.

stories.title: Detroit woman’s basement floods with sewage after city pipe work
stories.summary: Detroit resident Sharon Poindexter has dealt with sewage backing up into her basement since around Sept. 10, coinciding with city crews replacing lead service lines on her street. She says the situation worsens whenever her household uses water and that repeated calls to the city went nowhere. After WXYZ contacted Detroit Water and Sewerage Department, Deputy Director Sam Smalley said crews noticed a sewage smell near the lead line work and sent workers out to investigate and fix the issue.

photo.alt: Detroit woman’s basement floods with sewage after city pipe work

stories.title: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say
stories.summary: A 16-year-old victim revealed in an October 2025 interview that a man forced her to engage in sex acts between September and December 2024 while living in a house with him and Vukojevic. The teen confirmed in March 2026 that she was in videos showing forced sexual acts in a basement and upstairs bedroom, and that Vukojevic and others provided her with crack and crystal meth. Federal investigators confirmed these details through interviews and video evidence.

photo.alt: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say

stories.title: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say
stories.summary: Federal authorities allege a Detroit woman sexually exploited and trafficked a missing 16-year-old girl. Investigators identified the suspect, Jasmina Vukojevic, through a tattooed hand image and selfie-style photos on her phone. She is scheduled to appear in federal court on Oct. 27 for a status conference and has prior convictions for weapons and drug charges in Wayne and Macomb counties.

photo.alt: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say

stories.title: Detroit Zoo tax renewal goes before tri-county voters Nov. 3
stories.summary: Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties will vote Nov. 3 on renewing the Detroit Zoo’s property tax. The 10-year levy would raise $8.8 million annually for zoo operations and programs. Early voting starts Oct. 24, with the millage also supporting the Belle Isle Nature Center and school programs.

stories.title: DNR asks hunters to test deer for CWD in 5 Michigan counties
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources is requesting hunters to submit harvested deer from five counties for chronic wasting disease (CWD) testing during the 2026 hunting season. Samples from Mecosta, Newaygo, Kent, Montcalm, and Ionia counties will help assess disease progression since 2019. Testing results will inform management decisions to slow CWD's spread, which threatens deer populations but is not known to affect humans.

stories.title: DNR, Coast Guard rescue father, son who fell into Lake St. Clair
stories.summary: A father and son were rescued on Sept. 26 after becoming stranded in Lake St. Clair while setting a buoy course for a sailboat race. Both suffered hypothermia when a line tangled their boat's propeller, leading the father to enter the water to untangle it. The son later fell in and called 911, prompting a joint rescue effort by the Michigan DNR and Coast Guard.

stories.title: DNR commissions new Lake Michigan research vessel
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources has commissioned a new 66-foot, steel-hulled research vessel called the RV Steelhead to monitor Lake Michigan's fisheries and aquatic ecosystem. The vessel replaces an older DNR research vessel and includes safety and efficiency upgrades such as improved navigation equipment, a gyrostabilizer, and a solar charging system.

stories.title: DNR fire crews make progress against blazes. Are wildfires contained?
stories.summary: Michigan DNR firefighters are making slow progress against three wildfires in the western Upper Peninsula, with containment at 57%, 30%, and 50% for the Craig Lake, Dead River Basin, and Black River fires respectively. Challenges include rainy conditions, difficult terrain, and drought-affected deep-burning fires. The Craig Lake fire was caused by lightning, while the Ridge Fire's cause remains under investigation.

photo.alt: Wildfire burning in the Upper Peninsula with smoke rising from a ridge

stories.title: DNR makes progress against U.P. fires. Are they contained?
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources reported significant progress against three Upper Peninsula wildfires on Oct. 16, with two fires over 70% contained. The Clark Lake Fire near Craig Lake State Park and Black Lake Fire are each 70% contained, while the Ridge Fire near Dead River Basin is 40% contained. Firefighters are managing all three under the Rugged Terrain Complex, aided by recent rain reducing fire spread risks.

stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed noticeable improvements in all subjects and grades compared to 2019, with 7.6 percentage point growth in eighth-grade English proficiency and 6.8 percentage point growth in seventh-grade math. Despite a small dip in sixth-grade proficiency rates attributed to unfinished learning during the pandemic, the district's seventh-grade cohort outperformed peers, and SAT results also showed increases in English and math benchmarks.

photo.alt: DPSCD Continues Long-Term Improvement on 2026 M-STEP Results

stories.title: DPSCD continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) reported academic progress attributed to investments in teacher recruitment, evidence-based curriculum, student interventions, and wraparound services. The district has used funds from a $94.4 million literacy lawsuit settlement to hire interventionists and expand tutoring, though budget challenges loom as those funds expire. Experts note the improvements may reflect coordinated strategies rather than a single factor, with chronic absenteeism rates declining but still high at 60.9%.

stories.title: DPSCD: Funding Gaps Hinder Meeting Needs of English Learners
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) received $6.7 million in additional funds for over 7,400 English learners during the 2025-26 school year but did not receive funding for 1,041 students scoring 4.0 or higher on assessments. The district has used literacy lawsuit funds to hire 58 multilingual intervention specialists, but critics argue these roles do not replace required English language development minutes. Performance gaps persist, with only 10.4% of English learners meeting or exceeding proficiency in English on the 2025 MSTEP test, and a 79.2% four-year graduation rate, 3.8 percentage points below the district average.

photo.alt: Students in a classroom setting

stories.title: DPSCD: Las brechas de financiamiento dificultan satisfacer las necesidades de los estudiantes
stories.summary: El distrito escolar Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) no recibió fondos adicionales para 1.041 estudiantes que aprenden inglés con puntuaciones altas en evaluaciones, lo que refleja una brecha en el financiamiento estatal. El superintendente Nikolai Vitti criticó esta política, señalando que los estudiantes cercanos al dominio del inglés aún necesitan apoyo. A pesar de esfuerzos del distrito, persisten desafíos en el rendimiento académico y el acceso a servicios especializados para estos estudiantes.

stories.title: DPSCD’s new policy
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has adopted a new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs, requiring documentation for early pickups and prohibiting them in the final 30 minutes of the school day. Parents will face mandatory meetings and attendance contracts if their children have multiple unexcused departures, with consequences including chronic absenteeism tracking and potential grade repetition.

Seventh graders outperformed peers, and SAT proficiency rates increased by 6.6% in English and 4.3% in math. Smaller class sizes and interventions for ninth graders are expected to drive further growth.

stories.title: DPSCD superintendent addresses parent concerns on special education, communication, and accountability

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) teacher contract has been approved, including new guidelines on AI use in classrooms, lead teacher roles, and updated policies on maternity/paternity leave. While speech pathologist Michelle Awesome supports the leave policy, she criticizes the bonus system for exceeding caseload limits. The contract also adjusts transfer windows and professional development compensation rates.

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval - Chalkbeat

The contract prohibits AI from replacing teacher judgment in grading or assessments and introduces a $3,000 annual stipend for lead teachers in core subjects. Additional changes include expanded leave protections and adjusted compensation for professional development workshops.

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) teacher contract has been approved, introducing new guidelines on AI use in classrooms, lead teacher roles with stipends, and updated professional development rates. The agreement includes provisions for AI tools to support instruction but prohibits their use in grading or discipline decisions. Other highlights involve a revised voluntary transfer window, sick day restoration for parents returning from leave, and allowances for religious observance absences. Speech pathologist Michelle Awesome praised some aspects but criticized the bonus system for exceeding caseload limits.

stories.title: DPSCD to roll out high school redesign focusing on career pathways for ninth graders
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) will implement a high school redesign this fall, with ninth graders at 11 neighborhood high schools exploring career pathways through a seminar class. The initiative includes smaller class sizes, additional tutoring for students behind in literacy, and hiring seven more counselors to achieve a 1:250 student-counselor ratio. stories.title: Drought shrinks harvest at Romulus pumpkin farm, but visitors keep coming
stories.summary: A prolonged drought hurt this year’s harvest at a Romulus pumpkin farm, where owner Cyril Bird says the overall crop is down about 30%. Rain that giant pumpkins need in June and July never came, leaving the farm with roughly 600 to 700 pumpkins instead of the usual 1,000-plus. Irrigation couldn’t fully make up the difference. Still, visitors are turning out during the busy fall season, and Bird is hoping for dry weather now and better conditions next year.

The company claims this investment helped restore power to 90% of customers within 48 hours after a recent storm and reduced outage durations by 91% from 2023 to 2025. stories.title: DTE-funded group loses appeal to block Ann Arbor for Public Power ballot proposal

The Michigan Court of Appeals upheld the city clerk's certification of signatures, rejecting claims that supplemental submissions violated state law. The proposal, which would allow voters to decide on transitioning to a publicly owned utility system, will remain on the 2026 midterm ballot.

The amount of the new request, expected to be filed around Nov. 13, hasn’t been disclosed. Attorney General Dana Nessel criticized the timing as part of an 'unsustainable cycle' of rate cases. DTE says the notice is a required procedural step and won’t immediately affect bills, and said details on gas system investments are coming in November.

stories.title: End foreign wars
stories.summary: Trump promised to end foreign conflicts like the Ukraine-Russia war and Middle East chaos. While he halted direct aid to Ukraine, the US launched air strikes against Iran in February 2026, escalating Middle East tensions. The US has spent $37.5 billion on these attacks and deployed thousands of troops to the region.

stories.title: End inflation, lower interest, boost economy
stories.summary: Trump promised to end inflation and boost the economy through tax cuts and deregulation. While unemployment has slightly decreased, inflation remains at 3.4% (up from 3.0% when Trump took office) and mortgage rates remain high at 7%. Upper-income residents have benefited from stock market gains, but lower-income households have seen little improvement.

photo.alt: President Donald Trump dances to the 'Y.M.C.A' after delivering remarks on the economy and auto industry at the General Motors Proving Grounds in Milford, Michigan on Monday, July 27, 2026.

stories.title: End inflation, lower interest, boost economy
stories.summary: Trump promised to end inflation and boost Michigan's economy through tax cuts and deregulation. However, inflation remains at 3.4% as of August 2026, with food prices up 6-7% and mortgage rates at 7%. While the stock market has risen 22%, wage growth (3.6% in Michigan) lags behind national averages.

photo.alt: A meat counter at a grocery store.

stories.title: Energy prices and policies
stories.summary: Trump promised to cut energy costs in half by 2026 through fossil fuel expansion and ending EV subsidies. However, Michigan's gas prices have doubled to $4.91 per gallon, and diesel reached $6.81 per gallon. The US attacks on Iran and global events have disrupted energy markets despite record oil production.

photo.alt: President Donald Trump dances to the 'Y.M.C.A' after delivering remarks on the economy and auto industry at the General Motors Proving Grounds in Milford, Michigan on Monday, July 27, 2026.

stories.title: Energy prices and policy
stories.summary: Trump promised to cut energy costs in half by 2026 but Michigan's gas prices reached $4.91/gallon (up 80% from 2025) and diesel hit $6.81. The administration ended EV subsidies, saving $300 billion by 2035, but renewable energy still comprises 30% of US electricity. A $57 million loan aims to restart Michigan's Palisades nuclear plant.

photo.alt: President Donald Trump holds up his signed bill.

stories.title: Energy Prices in Michigan Rise Despite Trump's Promises

stories.title: Fact check: Did Jocelyn Benson ‘ignore’ laws, lose election lawsuits?

The shower is expected to peak overnight Oct. 21-22 and will be active until Nov. 7.

Campbell Coal Plant in West Olive, Michigan, ruling the agency exceeded its emergency authority. The plant, owned by Consumers Energy, was scheduled to close in 2025 but had its operations extended by the Trump administration. The court emphasized states' authority to regulate in-state power plants and rejected the DOE's justification for keeping the plant open. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel and environmental groups challenged the order, which is expected to save residents $600 million by 2040.

The case alleged the companies conspired to suppress renewable energy competition, but Judge Jane M. Nessel's office said it is reviewing the decision and considering next steps.

stories.summary: Firefighters contained an equipment fire at a manufacturing plant near Flint on Friday night. stories.title: Fire forced this beloved Grand Rapids Mexican restaurant to close: How it’s surviving
stories.summary: A fire in July destroyed the 7 Mares restaurant in Grand Rapids, forcing its closure. The Santoyo family reopened as a food truck across from the original location at 1403 Kalamazoo Ave. SE while awaiting insurance settlements and rebuilding. The food truck has become a temporary lifeline, allowing the family to maintain income and experiment with new menu items like birria egg rolls. The restaurant, founded in 1999, remains committed to reopening despite financial and logistical challenges.

photo.alt: After devastating fire, beloved Mexican restaurant 7 Mares has returned as food truck across from the restaurant, 1403 Kalamazoo Ave. SE, in Grand Rapids, Mich.

stories.title: Firefighters contain Upper Peninsula wildfire likely sparked by lightning strikes
stories.summary: Water-scooping aircraft from Minnesota are assisting Michigan firefighters in battling a 16-acre wildfire in Baraga County, Michigan, likely caused by lightning strikes. The fire, discovered near Craig Lake, has remained stable in size since its discovery on Thursday. Two planes from Hibbing, Minnesota, and a Michigan State Police helicopter are working the blaze, while DNR crews focus on containment amid high wind warnings. Authorities urge the public to avoid the area and keep drones grounded to ensure fire suppression operations can proceed safely.

stories.title: Firefighters make progress against U.P. blazes. What's happening now
stories.summary: Cooler temperatures and higher humidity have slowed two wildfires in Michigan's Upper Peninsula that burned for at least four days. The Ridge Fire near Marquette and Craig Lake Fire in Baraga are now 20% and 25% contained respectively. An evacuation order for areas south of the fires has been lifted, though an air quality alert remains in effect for multiple counties due to smoke.

stories.summary: New state rules restrict wireless devices during instruction and require fitness tests in gym classes. Michigan will provide free school meals to all public school students, and the SAT essay exam has been eliminated. Detroit leaders are expanding programs to reduce chronic absenteeism, including free bus service, rideshare options, and incentives for perfect attendance.

photo.alt: First day excitement as metro Detroit students head back to school

stories.summary: The University of Michigan will host the First Generation Symposium on Nov. 3, 2026, to discuss strategies for supporting first-generation students. The event, themed 'Shaped in Practice: Powered by Partnership,' includes a keynote by Rashné Jehangir and collaborative sessions. The Michigan League will also serve as a polling location on the same day, with attendees advised to plan for potential delays.

stories.summary: Five of seven seats on the Detroit Public Schools Community District Board are up for election with 31 candidates vying for four full four-year terms and three for a partial term. Board Vice President Bishop Corletta Vaughn, who is not seeking re-election, emphasized the need for community partnerships to address student needs beyond the classroom. Parents and advocates stress the importance of the election in shaping the district's future.

stories.summary: Pedestrian and bicycle safety advocates in Ann Arbor demanded immediate improvements to dangerous streets during a ride and rally at city hall on Sept. 22. They urged the City Council to address safety concerns and implement changes to protect cyclists and pedestrians.

stories.summary: Flash floods in late June 2026 caused washouts and road closures on M-119, with MDOT reporting damage at Middle Village Road, Devil's Elbow, South Lamkin Road, and Horseshoe Bend. Water damage was also reported at Middle Village Road.

stories.title: Flint aims to cut cancer deaths in half with early-detection initiative
stories.summary: Flint has announced an initiative to reduce cancer deaths by 50% over the next decade through early detection technology. The city, in partnership with healthcare industry leaders, aims to expand access to advanced diagnostics and has launched a study involving over 400 residents. Local leaders emphasized Flint's role as the first 'Early Detection City' in the U.S. and highlighted the importance of equitable healthcare access.

photo.alt: Flint Mayor Sheldon Neeley speaks alongside local leaders and healthcare industry partners during a new conference on Friday, Oct. 2, that was livestreamed on Facebook. During the conference, Neeley discussed an ongoing initiative aimed at reducing cancer deaths in the city by 50%.

stories.title: Flint council committee rejects school fighting ordinance
stories.summary: Flint's legislative committee rejected a proposed ordinance aimed at reducing school violence and addressing chronic absenteeism through penalties and community service requirements. The 5-1 vote followed concerns about overreach and existing state regulations, though Councilwoman Ladel Lewis expressed hope to revisit the issue. The ordinance was inspired by a similar law in Grand Blanc adopted in March 2025.

photo.alt: Flint City Council Chambers at Flint City Hall, located at 1101 S. Saginaw St.

stories.title: Flint man convicted after rifle with 45-round drum found in traffic stop
stories.summary: A 36-year-old Flint man was convicted of being a felon in possession of a firearm after a rifle with a 45-round drum magazine was found in his vehicle during a traffic stop. Jamal Allen Johnson received four additional felony convictions, including operating while intoxicated and having an open container of alcohol. He faces up to life in prison when sentenced on October 13, 2026.

photo.alt: Genesee County Circuit Courthouse

stories.title: Flint man partially convicted in shooting that left teen paralyzed
stories.summary: A 23-year-old Flint man was partially convicted of firing into a home and seriously injuring a 17-year-old girl during a March 23, 2025, Flint Township shooting. Mario Devon White, Jr., was found guilty of discharging a firearm causing serious impairment, felony firearm, and domestic violence charges, but acquitted of assault with intent to murder. The shooting left the teen paralyzed after bullets struck her home, with sentencing set for November 9.

photo.alt: The Genesee County Circuit Courthouse is pictured.

stories.title: Flint partners with Consumers Energy to add bill payment option at Clio Road service center
stories.summary: The City of Flint is adding in-person Consumers Energy bill payment services at its Clio Road service center following the utility’s planned closure of its local payment office on Nov. 30. The new service aims to maintain accessibility for residents, with details on start dates and procedures to be announced later. Mayor Sheldon A. Neeley emphasized the city’s commitment to accessible services for Flint residents.

photo.alt: Flint partners with Consumers Energy to add bill payment option at Clio Road service center

stories.summary: An adult male was found dead in the parking lot of American Inn after a report of a shooting, police said. The Flint Police Department responded to the reported shooting at 4 a.m. on Oct. 9. The victim suffered gunshot injuries in the parking lot of the 2701 N. Dort Highway hotel, with no suspect information provided and the deceased's identity unreleased.

stories.title: Flint sushi restaurant co-owner released from ICE custody on bond
stories.summary: Salman Fnu, co-owner of Kabuki Japanese Restaurant in Flint, was released from ICE custody on a $5,000 bond after being detained on Sept. 25. His attorney, Rachel Glogowski, stated the family is 'delighted' to be reunited, though the immigration case will continue. The restaurant temporarily closed during his detention, and his wife Ashley Parker had filed marriage-based immigration paperwork in 2024.

photo.alt: Co-owners Salman Fnu and Ashley Parker pose for a portrait on Thursday, April 17, 2025, at Kabuki Japanese Restaurant in Flint. The restaurant is located at 4018 Corunna Road.

stories.title: Flint Township mom pleads guilty after sons, ages 3 and 4, found abandoned in condo
stories.summary: Krystal Farmer, a Flint Township woman, pleaded guilty to multiple charges including child abandonment and abuse after her two young sons with disabilities were found in deplorable conditions inside a condominium in February 2026. The guilty plea was entered on September 21, 2026, with sentencing scheduled for October 19. Officers discovered the children unsupervised in a residence filled with standing water, trash, and feces.

photo.alt: Flint Township police vehicle in a file photo. (Jake May | MLive.com)

stories.title: Flint Township set to begin road resurfacing program Sept. 21

stories.title: Flock is catching flak. Experts say other police surveillance tools are more worrisome
stories.summary: Privacy experts warn that easy-to-use police surveillance tools like Flock cameras reduce friction in investigations, increasing risks of misuse and mass surveillance. While law enforcement argues such tools help solve crimes, critics highlight potential for abuse, including targeting specific groups or individuals. Legal scholars urge proactive measures like data retention limits and audits to address constitutional concerns.

photo.alt: A solar-powered security camera on a metal pole

stories.title: Flying out of Detroit Metro? Expect to pay more
stories.summary: Average domestic airfare at Detroit Metro Airport reached $527 in the second quarter, a $108 increase from the previous year. Rising jet fuel costs, labor expenses, strong travel demand, and limited nonstop competition on some routes are contributing to higher ticket prices. Travelers report increased costs for family visits and trips home.

photo.alt: Flying out of Detroit Metro? Expect to pay more

stories.title: Food banks strained as Michigan SNAP rolls shrink, hotline calls surge
stories.summary: Michigan has about 167,000 fewer SNAP recipients than a year ago, a nearly 13% drop since the federal budget law was signed, and advocates link it to tougher work and eligibility rules. The state must absorb roughly $94 million more in administrative costs and could face $400 million more in costs next year because its error rate tops 9%. Food banks report surging demand, and they are urging Congress to extend the deadline for meeting the 6% error threshold.

photo.alt: Avatar photo

stories.summary: A food hub initiative in Jackson will receive a $25,000 donation from Chelsea State Bank to support the River & Rail Food Hub. The new grocery and cafe in the former state prison aims to connect consumers with locally sourced food and strengthen the regional food system. Grow Jackson recently opened the facility, with funds designated to expand access to fresh food and create community partnerships.

stories.summary: Every Friday through September 25, County Farm Park hosts food trucks offering coffee, pizza, tacos, sandwiches, and burgers from 11am-7pm. stories.summary: Pro-Palestinian activists at the University of Michigan report ongoing repercussions such as disciplinary actions and campus bans, despite dropped criminal charges. The 2024 encampment raid led to arrests and allegations of differential treatment compared to pro-Israel protesters.

stories.title: ‘For you, this is just a game’: Ypsilanti Township residents push back against planned data center at UMich town hall
stories.summary: Residents of Ypsilanti Township expressed opposition to the University of Michigan's planned data center during a town hall meeting, citing environmental and community impact concerns. Attendees criticized the University for lack of transparency and potential environmental racism, while university officials defended the project's necessity and feasibility.

stories.title: Force Detroit leader urges gun safety after 11-year-old shot on Detroit’s west side
stories.summary: Eyvette Hansberry of Force Detroit urges gun owners to secure firearms after an 11-year-old was shot on Detroit's west side. photo.alt: Force Detroit leader urges gun safety after 11-year-old shot on Detroit’s west side

stories.title: Foreign policy experts criticize U.S. involvement in the Middle East at Ford panel
stories.summary: Foreign policy experts at a Ford panel discussion criticized U.S. military and political involvement in the Middle East, arguing for a reevaluation of foreign policy strategies. The panel highlighted historical consequences of interventionist policies and called for increased diplomatic efforts over military action.

photo.alt: Foreign policy experts criticize U.S. involvement in the Middle East at Ford panel

stories.title: Forgotten Harvest Farms races to harvest 1 million pounds of food
stories.summary: The food rescue nonprofit Forgotten Harvest aims to harvest 1 million pounds of produce by year-end through volunteer efforts at its Detroit-area farm. Volunteers plant, weed, and harvest crops like cabbage, with recent efforts yielding over 10,000 pounds. The food is distributed via mobile pantries to ensure fresh produce reaches those in need within days of harvest.

photo.alt: Volunteers at the Forgotten Harvest Farms in Fenton, Michigan

stories.title: Former Ann Arbor pastor accused of sexual abuse
stories.summary: A former Ann Arbor pastor, Seth Kim, is accused of sexual abuse by multiple women, including Survivor A (Jane Doe) and Survivor B. The Harvest Mission Community Church issued a statement on October 11, 2026, acknowledging the allegations and removing Kim from leadership roles. A third woman has also come forward with similar claims, though no criminal charges have been filed against Kim in Washtenaw County.
entities: University of Michigan Division of Public Safety and Security

stories.title: Former Bridgeport-Spaulding schools superintendent sues district
stories.summary: A former superintendent of Bridgeport-Spaulding Community School District filed a federal lawsuit alleging wrongful termination and constitutional violations, seeking more than $25,000 in damages. The 31-page lawsuit names the district, its board president, and multiple board members, containing 12 counts including breach of contract and violations of state and federal law. The board appointed an interim superintendent the day before the lawsuit was filed.

photo.alt: Bridgeport High School at 4961 Bearcat Blvd.Cole Waterman

stories.title: Former Detroit USPS worker sentenced to 20 months for unemployment fraud
stories.summary: Former Detroit postal worker Christopher Powell, 37, was sentenced to 20 months in federal prison for fraudulently obtaining over $166,000 in unemployment benefits. Powell admitted to submitting fraudulent unemployment insurance claims in multiple states from July 2020 through January 2024 and directing related mail to an address on his postal delivery route. He pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud and was ordered to pay $166,366.53 in restitution.
entities: U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General
U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General

stories.title: Former Holland judge sentenced to fines after throwing items from bench at defendant
stories.summary: A former Holland District Judge Bradley S. Knoll was sentenced to fines and costs for a misdemeanor assault and battery charge. The incident occurred on Feb. 13 during a landlord-tenant dispute when Knoll allegedly threw self-inking stamps from the bench at a defendant. Knoll retired months earlier than expected in 2026 under a state Supreme Court consent order following prior legal issues, including a 2023 domestic violence investigation.

stories.title: Former Jackson County sheriff’s deputy accused of sexually assaulting 3 girls

Two women and a minor testified against him during a preliminary examination on Sept. 29, 2026, leading to the case being sent to Circuit Court. Strawser, 27, was fired in November 2023 after withholding information about prior allegations during his hiring process.

stories.title: Former Metro Detroit doctor sentenced to 9 years in multi-state child porn case
stories.summary: A former Metro Detroit doctor who pleaded guilty in May to a federal child pornography charge was sentenced to nine years in prison. Lincoln Erickson, 32, was arrested in December as part of a multi-state investigation that also led to the arrest of three other men. The FBI found child sexual abuse material on Erickson's phone and evidence of coordinated predatory behavior among the suspects.

photo.alt: Former Michigan hockey players sue university, allege years of sexualized hazing and abuse

stories.title: Former Michigan House speaker slated for Sept. 21 trial amid accusations of misusing political funds
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield is set for a Sept. 21 trial on 13 felony charges, including criminal enterprise and embezzlement, related to misuse of funds from his political action committees and the Peninsula Fund. His wife Stephanie was recently sentenced for embezzling from the same fund, while the attorney general's office closed a prior sexual assault investigation due to insufficient evidence. The case involves testimony from former aides and allegations of improper mileage reimbursements and personal use of social welfare organization funds.

stories.title: Former Michigan Strategic Fund board member blasts decision to fund UP’s Copperwood Mine
stories.summary: A former Michigan Strategic Fund board member criticized the allocation of $50 million to support the Copperwood Mine in the Western Upper Peninsula, arguing that the board used funds from previously approved projects and bypassed legislative requirements. The company had not secured required financing two years after initial approval.

stories.title: Freaks and Geeks
stories.summary: Forever remembered as one of the great non-starters of ’90s television, creator Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow’s sublime “Freaks and Geeks” now exists as one of the most effortlessly perfect things ever created. Set in a fictional Detroit suburb in the year 1980, the show stars Lindsay Weir (Linda Cardellini) and her younger brother Sam (John Francis Daley) as they navigate the awkwardness of high school. Lindsay hangs out with freaks and burnouts: there’s Nick (Jason Segel), the Rush-obsessed aspiring drummer, and Kim (Busy Philipps), the mean girl from a bad part of town. Meanwhile, Sam is an awkward geek who spends most of his time with fellow nerds Neal (Samm Levine) and Bill (Martin Starr). It’s hard to imagine why the show was ever cancelled: Every episode is a treasure trove of [pitch-perfect comedy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dB_D_ZxGUWA) and [surprisingly tender moments](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmCpmEQD0L4), featuring nearly every important comedy actor of the aughts and 2010s (no, [really](https://www.looper.com/820224/famous-actors-you-forgot-showed-up-on-freaks-and-geeks/)). Watch it now for an inviting fall atmosphere, a sneaky University of Michigan reference (“I mean, are the kids in Michigan schools that stupid?” might be the best line in the show) and one of the greatest finales in TV history.

stories.title: Gilmore Girls
stories.summary: There is no show as synonymous with fall as “Gilmore Girls.” Though the series concluded nearly two decades ago, fans annually rewatch all 153 episodes when summer ends. Following its resurgence with Generation Z, the Lorelais (mother-daughter co-protagonists who share the same name) returned for a renewal miniseries, “Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life,” in 2016, but nothing holds up quite like the original. From Chilton Preparatory School to Yale University, follow Rory Gilmore’s (Alexis Bledel) journey through high school romance, friendship and rivalry, college applications and university life. While she’s funny, relatable and occasionally frustrating, the best part of Rory Gilmore is her heartwarming relationship with her mother, Lorelai (Lauren Graham), as she navigates growing up and finding independence. However, what truly keeps viewers coming back is the cozy, comforting atmosphere the show creates. Set in the small fictional town of Stars Hollow, Conn., the knit sweaters, pumpkin patches, cider mills and close-knit community perfectly embody the warmth of autumn. If you start the show today, you’ll watch the leaves turn and fall alongside the Gilmore girls, ready to do it all over again next year.

stories.title: Glacier Detachment in Nepal Triggers Floods in China and Nepal
stories.summary: A significant glacier detachment in Nepal on August 28, 2026, caused a flood that impacted downstream areas in both China and Nepal. The event, which mobilized material from a glacier at 5200 m a.s.l., met with previous flood deposits, leading to a dam failure and subsequent flooding. Satellite imagery and photos confirm the detachment and its effects.

stories.title: Great Lakes ice cover is shrinking fast. A century of data reveals why
stories.summary: A new study analyzing 125 years of data reveals that Great Lakes ice cover has declined rapidly over the past four decades, with a 10-fold faster rate of loss in the last 30-40 years. Researchers found that ice fluctuations are influenced by both climate change and a 60-year cyclical pattern linked to the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO). The findings highlight the importance of understanding these dynamics for managing regional ecosystems, fisheries, and coastal infrastructure.
entities: Cooperative Institute for Great Lakes Research

stories.title: Great Lakes lab hit by DOGE is hanging on — for now

Despite efforts to eliminate the lab entirely through budget proposals, GLERL continues to operate with funding largely intact due to congressional resistance. However, staff reductions have impaired its capacity for ecosystem research and public communication, according to former director Deborah Lee and current partners.

photo.alt: Jackson teen shot by police near fairgrounds undergoes surgery

stories.title: Jackson to showcase new Flatiron District housing development at open house
stories.summary: The City of Jackson and Norfolk Homes will host an open house on Oct. 8 to showcase homes under construction in the Flatiron District. The event replaces a previously canceled groundbreaking celebration and highlights the city's efforts to revitalize neighborhoods through new housing. City officials emphasized collaboration and infrastructure work in preparing the site for residential development.

photo.alt: Snow accumulates on the City of Jackson sign in Jackson on Saturday, Jan. 19, 2019.

stories.title: Jail partly evacuated during small fire in Monroe County
stories.summary: The Monroe County jail was partly evacuated on Sept. 21, 2026, after a small fire broke out in an unoccupied housing unit while contractors were working. No inmates were in the affected area, but a nearby occupied unit was evacuated as a precaution. The fire was quickly extinguished by jail staff and contractors, with assistance from the Monroe Department of Public Safety for smoke ventilation.

photo.alt: Police lights MLive

stories.title: Jaycee Park Playground Progress and ADA Features
stories.summary: Jaycee Park's playground installation is nearly complete with ADA entrance ramps included. Pathway connections will be finalized through an upcoming project.

stories.title: Jayden Perron scores first career hat trick in Michigan takedown of Alaska Anchorage
stories.summary: U-M hockey player Jayden Perron recorded his first career hat trick, leading Michigan to a decisive victory over Alaska Anchorage. The performance marked a career milestone and showcased the team’s offensive strength.

photo.alt: Jayden Perron scores first career hat trick in Michigan takedown of Alaska Anchorage

stories.title: JD Vance hitting the campaign trail in Michigan Thursday for GOP rally
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance will be the keynote speaker at a GOP campaign rally in Monroe, Michigan on Thursday afternoon. The event, starting at 2:45 p.m. at LevelUp Training Complex, comes amid a competitive U.S. Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed. Local road closures on Stewart Road will be in effect from 1-6 p.m. to accommodate the event.

photo.alt: Vice President JD Vance waving as he disembarks Air Force Two at Joint Base Andrews, Md., following a trip to Maine, Monday, Aug. 24, 2026

stories.title: JD Vance, Mike Rogers keep up attacks on Abdul El-Sayed during Monroe rally
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance and Republican candidate Mike Rogers intensified attacks on Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed during a Monroe rally, framing the race as a choice between 'common sense' and 'crazy' progressive policies. The event highlighted GOP policy proposals like property tax repeal while El-Sayed and Democrats accused Republicans of undermining Michiganders through cuts to social programs and foreign policy missteps.

photo.alt: Vice President JD Vance speaks at an event at a robotics manufacturing facility in Auburn Hills on March 18, 2026

stories.title: “Jekyll & Hyde: The Musical,” Oct. 22–25
stories.summary: Ann Arbor Civic Theatre launches its mainstage season with Frank Wildhorn’s dramatic musical adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic novel. The production follows Dr. Henry Jekyll’s dangerous experiment to separate the good and evil within humanity, resulting in the terrifying emergence of Edward Hyde. Featuring soaring music and gothic suspense, the production closes the month with one of musical theatre’s most enduring psychological thrillers.

stories.title: Jewish and Democratic leaders urge El-Sayed to address Israel concerns
stories.summary: Jewish and Democratic Party leaders in Michigan have called on Abdul El-Sayed to address concerns about his criticism of Israel. Cantor Regina Hyatt expressed feeling alienated by political rhetoric, with many Jewish voters considering sitting out the election. El-Sayed has defended his stance on Israel while emphasizing his support for Jewish community safety.

photo.alt: Jewish and Democratic leaders urge El-Sayed to address Israel concerns

stories.title: Jewish groups mark 3-year anniversary of deadly Oct. 7 attacks
stories.summary: In the third anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks in Israel, Oak Park's Jewish community center distributed memorial cards for each victim and held a remembrance event. The anniversary marks the first since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran. The attacks, coordinated by Hamas, killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

photo.alt: Portrait of Frank Witsil

stories.title: Jimmy Hoffa’s summer home now available for rent on Airbnb, Vrbo
stories.summary: Called ‘The Hoffa House,’ Jimmy Hoffa’s former lakefront summer home on Square Lake Road in Michigan is now available for short-term rentals. The property, linked to the unsolved mystery of Hoffa’s disappearance over 50 years ago, is filled with historical significance.

photo.alt: Jimmy Hoffa’s summer home now available for rent on Airbnb, Vrbo

stories.title: Job losses pile up in battleground states
stories.summary: The GOP faces backlash from factory workers in battleground states like Michigan, Iowa, and Kansas as Trump's tariffs lead to job losses and economic strain. Republican Bill Huizenga, running for re-election in Michigan, initially supported the tariffs but now faces criticism from constituents like Tracy Chew, who lost her job after a plant closure in Iowa. Companies such as Winnebago Industries and Vornado Air have cut jobs due to increased import costs, while Bombardier faces potential U.S. sales restrictions if it doesn't shift production.

stories.summary: Jocelyn Benson leads John James by over 7 points in Michigan's 2026 gubernatorial race according to recent polling. stories.title: Jocelyn Benson’s record: Election fights, faster DMV visits, transparency flop
stories.summary: Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, running for governor, highlights her administrative efficiency and voting rights advocacy, including faster DMV services and expanded voting options. Critics argue she has politicized her office and faced transparency issues, while her tenure has included legal disputes over elections and voter roll management. Benson defends her record as data-driven and focused on saving Michiganders time and protecting voting rights.

stories.title: Joe Louis Greenway extension, I-75 cap study win state money
stories.summary: Detroit will receive $13.25 million from a $23-million state investment announced Wednesday by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, the largest share among nine projects statewide. Most of it, $10.5 million, funds a new National Guard Readiness Center at the Olympia Armory. Another $2.5 million advances a Joe Louis Greenway segment linking Detroit and Highland Park, and $250,000 supports planning to cap parts of I-75. The money helps leverage federal grants. No construction timelines were announced.

stories.title: John James and Jocelyn Benson debate data center policies in Michigan gubernatorial race
stories.summary: During a gubernatorial debate, Jocelyn Benson and John James clashed over data center policies. Benson advocated for a moratorium and accused James of profiting from data centers, while James proposed a five-part moratorium with environmental guidelines and emphasized local control. Both candidates addressed concerns about resident involvement in data center decisions.

photo.alt: Gubernatorial debate between John James and Jocelyn Benson

stories.title: John James and Jocelyn Benson Discuss SNAP Benefits in Gubernatorial Debate
stories.summary: During a gubernatorial debate, John James and Jocelyn Benson discussed their plans to address potential cuts to Michigan's SNAP benefits. James emphasized protecting high-unemployment areas through waivers and reducing fraud, while Benson focused on making food affordable through partnerships with local farmers and criticized James for voting to cut benefits. James clarified he supported the Farm Bill to protect SNAP.

stories.title: John James Took Thousands from Poultry Executives Tied to Pollution, Labor Violations

The donations occurred during James' campaign for governor, with $8,325 from Mountaire Corporation chairman Ronnie Cameron and $3,000 from former Vande Bunte Eggs CEO Timothy Vande Bunte.

During a campaign stop in metro Detroit, James stated he would seek more oversight as governor, criticizing the current independence of the state board of education. His Democratic opponent, Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, also advocates for more resources for teachers and students.

stories.title: Judge decides who will bury newborn baby found dead at Electric Forest
stories.summary: A judge in Oceana County has appointed Travis Byrnes to arrange the burial of a newborn baby found dead at the Electric Forest Music Festival in Rothbury. Byrnes must cover burial expenses and provide a permanent grave marker at Georgetown Cemetery in Hudsonville. Leroy Strait had also petitioned for the responsibility, but the court chose Byrnes' proposal due to better accessibility for future family visits. The infant's mother remains unidentified, and the FBI is offering a $15,000 reward for information leading to the responsible party.

stories.title: Just 1 in 4 Michigan juniors are ‘college ready,’ SAT scores indicate
stories.summary: Only 25.3% of Michigan high school juniors are considered college ready based on SAT scores, marking a decline from previous years. The College Board defines college readiness as a 75% chance of earning at least a C in first-semester college courses. School leaders emphasize that metrics like Advanced Placement courses and career tech programs also reflect readiness.

photo.alt: A student takes a practice exam to prepare for the SAT. Statewide, 26.5% of students met the ‘college ready’ math benchmark during the 2025-2026 school year and 52.1% met the reading and writing mark. (AP Photo/Butch Dill)

stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Education's suspension of a comprehensive monitoring process has increased the risk of undetected waste, fraud, and abuse in K-12 funding, according to a Government Accountability Office report. The report also highlighted unreliable absenteeism data, with some schools reporting rates over 100%, and noted the lack of a timeline for resuming federal compliance reviews.

stories.title: K-2 reading growth slowed last year in the Detroit district. Here’s what administrators say caused it.
stories.summary: Reading growth for Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) students in kindergarten to second grade stalled in the 2025-26 school year, despite initial improvements from a $94.4 million literacy lawsuit settlement. Superintendent Nikolai Vitti attributed the slowdown to insufficient individualized interventions for students near grade level and challenges like undiagnosed disabilities, chronic absenteeism, and summer learning loss. The district’s results showed 27.3% of K-2 students were proficient in reading, up less than 1 percentage point from the previous year.

stories.title: Kalamazoo boil water advisory could lift Monday after clean test results

The city expects to end the advisory Monday, Sept. 21, if additional samples analyzed Monday morning also come back clean. Public Services staff are collecting those samples over the next 24 hours while crews continue flushing the water system and conducting additional checks.

stories.title: Kim Mathers permitted to leave jail for in-patient treatment, judge rules

stories.title: Labor Day Weekend: How Did Students Spend Their Break?
stories.summary: Students in the Ann Arbor school district used the Labor Day break for trips, festivals, work, and family gatherings. While some, like Ellie Ledbetter, traveled to New York City for college tours, others like Lila Sarnecki attended the Detroit Jazz Festival or worked, such as Wesley Saidak’s family celebration at a trailer park. Opinions on the break’s timing varied, with some appreciating the gradual return to school and others finding it disruptive.

stories.title: Labor Day Weekend: How Did Students Spend Their Break?
stories.summary: CHS students shared how they spent their Labor Day weekend break, which included college visits in New York City, attending the Detroit Jazz Festival, and family gatherings at a trailer park. The four-day break (Sept. 4-7) allowed students to ease back into the school year after a short first week. While opinions varied on the break's timing, all students used the time to its fullest potential.

stories.title: Lack of ‘moral outrage’ over Islamophobia is helping normalize religious hate, advocates say
stories.summary: As Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed faces Islamophobic attacks during his campaign, advocates warn that the lack of condemnation from political leaders is normalizing religious hate. Far-right figures like Jake Lang and lawmakers such as Mike Rogers have amplified anti-Muslim rhetoric, while experts note a 1,900% surge in Islamophobic content targeting El-Sayed after his primary win. Scholars and civil rights leaders argue that Islamophobia has become politically acceptable, with calls for stronger opposition to religious bigotry from both parties.
entities: Center for the Study of Organized Hate

stories.summary: The modern campground at Lake Gogebic State Park in Marenisco is closed through June 7, 2027, for the removal of around 800 trees infested by an invasive species.

stories.title: Lake Orion village disincorporation petition stalls amid legal dispute
stories.summary: A citizen-led effort to dissolve Lake Orion village has stalled after county officials declined to place the disincorporation question on the ballot, leading to a lawsuit and appeal. The dispute centers on tax rates and governance, with residents arguing that maintaining the village creates duplicate services and higher taxes. A judge dismissed the initial lawsuit, but the case remains unresolved as the county election commission cannot consider the petition due to legal challenges.

photo.alt: Historic district sign in downtown Lake Orion

stories.title: Lansing police investigating ‘commonalities’ of 5 homeless deaths along city’s River Trail
stories.summary: Lansing police are investigating potential links between five homeless deaths along the city’s River Trail in the past year, with three ruled homicides and others under investigation. Chief Robert Backus stated detectives are examining similarities, including victims being homeless, assaults occurring during early morning hours, and facial/head injuries. A tip line and increased police patrols have been implemented.

photo.alt: Lansing Police Chief Robert Backus discussing River Trail deaths

stories.title: Lansing protesters block Flock cameras over license plate reader contract
stories.summary: Lansing residents and activist groups are pressuring the city to terminate its contract with Flock Safety over privacy concerns. The Lansing City Council voted 7-1 in August to request the city end the contract, but Mayor Andy Schor has not acted, citing contractual obligations. Protesters physically blocked Flock cameras at a major intersection on Sept. 28, 2026, while advocating for a citywide ban on automated license plate readers. Similar cancellations of Flock contracts are occurring across Michigan as critics highlight potential misuse of the technology.

photo.alt: A sign reading 'Flock Out!' blocks a Flock license plate reader camera in Lansing, Mich. on Sept. 28, 2026.

stories.title: Lansing protesters block Flock cameras over license plate reader contract
stories.summary: Lansing residents, including members of DeFlock Lansing and the Michigan Capitol Visibility Brigade, protested at a major intersection to block Flock Safety's automated license plate reader cameras. The Lansing City Council voted 7-1 to request termination of the contract due to privacy concerns, but Mayor Andy Schor has not yet acted. Protesters argue the technology violates privacy rights and cite misuse cases, including police abuse of Flock data.

photo.alt: Protestors from DeFlock Lansing hold signs to block automated license plate reader cameras at the intersection of Pennsylvania Ave. and Michigan Ave. in Lansing on Sept. 28, 2026. (Photo by Kyle Davidson/Michigan Advance)

stories.summary: A boil water advisory affecting much of Kalamazoo was lifted on Sept. 21, 2026, after the city confirmed the water is safe to drink. The advisory was issued on Sept. 19 following the detection of E. coli and coliform bacteria in the water supply. Residents and businesses were advised to boil water during the advisory period.

stories.title: Last of Hastings apartment units evacuated over ricin incident now cleared for reentry
stories.summary: Health officials have cleared all areas of the Tyden Lofts apartment complex in Hastings, MI, for reoccupation following a ricin-related evacuation on Sept. 10. While most units were accessible by Sept. 14, first-floor units remained restricted until now. A 24-year-old man, Joseph Jay Sheppard, faces charges related to the incident, which involved the illegal possession and use of ricin, a deadly poison derived from castor beans.

stories.title: Lawrence faults Barrett over Medicaid cuts, renews Medicare for All push
stories.summary: Political organizer William Lawrence criticized Republican Congressman Tom Barrett for Medicaid cuts under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which requires work requirements and more frequent eligibility checks starting 2027. Lawrence, running against Barrett, argued these changes will increase the uninsured population and push for Medicare for All as an alternative. Barrett countered that his policies aim to reduce healthcare costs and improve drug price transparency.

stories.title: Lawrence launches ‘Michigan First’ constituency services plan highlighting Barrett town hall woes
stories.summary: Democratic Congressional candidate William Lawrence has unveiled a five-point ‘Michigan First’ constituency services plan targeting U.S. Rep. Tom Barrett’s lack of in-person town halls during his tenure. The plan includes quarterly in-district town halls, mobile and virtual office hours, faster response times, and dedicated support for veterans and seniors. Barrett’s campaign criticized Lawrence for organizing protests before Barrett’s first vote, while Lawrence’s tour promoting the plan will visit multiple cities in October.

stories.title: Lawrence M. Seiford to Retire from University of Michigan
stories.summary: Lawrence M. Seiford, professor of industrial and operations engineering, will retire on May 24, 2026. He joined U-M in 2000 and served as department chair and co-director of the Tauber Institute. His research in operations research and data envelopment analysis earned him numerous awards and fellowships.

stories.summary: Paige Shiver, a former Michigan football department employee, filed a lawsuit against the University of Michigan, alleging the university improperly denied public records requests related to Sherrone Moore's termination. The lawsuit claims violations of Michigan's FOIA law and includes allegations of sex discrimination and privacy violations. The university declined to comment when contacted by Local 4 in July.

stories.title: Lawsuit Alleges Blue Cross Antitrust Violations in Michigan Health Insurance Market
stories.summary: A lawsuit alleges that Blue Cross violated Sections 1 and 2 of the Sherman Act and Michigan Antitrust Reform Act by participating in horizontal agreements to monopolize the large group health insurance market in Michigan and restrict healthcare service purchases from providers. The case seeks permanent injunctions against anticompetitive conduct and treble damages for supracompetitive pricing. The document was filed on October 8, 2026, in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

stories.title: Lawsuit alleges MDOC staff filmed incarcerated woman while giving birth, violating privacy statute
stories.summary: A lawsuit filed Oct. 8, 2025, alleges eight Michigan Department of Corrections employees violated the privacy of Natalie Forrest by recording her on body cameras during childbirth at Women’s Huron Valley Correctional Facility on March 8, 2025. The complaint claims the filming violated Michigan’s voyeurism statute, despite being notified of the policy’s illegality on Feb. 17, 2025. Forrest described the experience as degrading, impacting her mental health and ability to bond with her newborn, while attorneys argue the practice treats incarcerated women as 'subhuman.'

photo.alt: Women’s Huron Valley Correctional Facility in Saline Township, Michigan. | Photo by Jon King/Michigan Advance

stories.title: Lee Chatfield embezzlement trial delayed over expert witness dispute
stories.summary: An Ingham County judge delayed the corruption trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges for allegedly misusing funds from a political nonprofit and campaign committees. The delay allows Chatfield's attorney to appeal a decision permitting testimony from a state-aligned forensic accountant. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel criticized the delay as 'outrageous,' while defense attorney Mary Chartier accused the state of poor scheduling and 'disrespect' toward the courts.

photo.alt: Lee Chatfield testifying in court (U.P. Politico / Wikimedia Commons)

stories.title: Lee Chatfield embezzlement trial delayed over expert witness dispute
stories.summary: An Ingham County judge delayed the corruption trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield to allow his attorney to appeal a decision permitting testimony from a state-aligned forensic accountant. The defense argues the witness' expertise is irrelevant to the case, while Attorney General Dana Nessel accused the courts of stalling. The appeals process could extend beyond Nessel's tenure in office.

stories.title: Lee Chatfield trial delayed again, this time over disputed expert witness
stories.summary: Lee Chatfield’s trial was delayed again after his attorney appealed a judge’s decision to allow a forensic accountant as an expert witness. The appeal could push the trial into 2027, after Attorney General Dana Nessel leaves office, and centers on disputed financial reports. Chatfield faces 13 felony counts related to alleged embezzlement from 2020-2021, including funding personal expenses through political fundraising accounts.

stories.title: Legacy Costs Appropriations for FY2027

stories.title: Legacy Gallery
stories.summary: The Legacy Gallery at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum features exhibits like the Ferrofluid Magnetoscope by local artist Michael Flynn, along with interactive activities including giant soap bubbles, HAM radio, and Morse code exploration. stories.title: Legal Case Alleges Antitrust Conspiracy Among Health Insurance Providers
stories.summary: A federal court filing alleges that Blue Cross and Blue Shield affiliates, along with other companies, conspired to restrict competition through revenue-sharing rules and geographic market allocation. The complaint details three key agreements limiting revenue from non-Blue Cross services, enforcing local market dominance, and preventing cross-territory provider contracts. The case was filed on October 8, 2026, in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

stories.title: Legislative Directed Spending Reporting Mandated
stories.summary: The Michigan legislature must submit a jointly agreed-upon list of legislatively directed spending items to the state budget office within 30 days of enactment. Agencies must publicly report grant details by March 15, June 15, and September 15 of the fiscal year.

stories.title: Legislatively Directed Spending Items Must Be Publicly Disclosed
stories.summary: The legislature must submit a list of legislatively directed spending items to the state budget office within 30 days of the act's effective date. Departments must also post and update reports on these items by March 15, June 15, and September 15 each fiscal year.

stories.title: Legislature Intends to Fund Native American Tuition Waivers for Public Universities
stories.summary: For the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, the Michigan legislature intends to allocate funds for unfunded North American Indian tuition waiver costs at public universities. A report on these waivers, including application numbers and student enrollment data, must be submitted by January 15 of each year.

stories.title: Less jeering, just as much emotion at second U-M town hall on proposed computing center
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's second town hall about its controversial computing center in Ypsilanti Township drew opponents with less jeering but high emotion. Residents criticized the project as 'environmental racism' and raised concerns about noise, pollution, and quality of life, while university officials defended the site's industrial zone location and denied environmental impacts. Ypsilanti Township Supervisor Brenda Stumbo called for the project to be stopped and announced plans for her own town hall.

photo.alt: U of M Professor Steven Ceccio explaining the computing center at a town hall.

stories.title: Lessons from Detroit’s ShotStoppers Community Violence Intervention Program
stories.summary: The City of Detroit’s ShotStoppers program, launched in 2023, funds community-based organizations to reduce gun violence through targeted interventions and community engagement. Evaluations show decreases in homicides and non-fatal shootings in designated zones, with teams using strategies like individual outreach and resource provision. Trust and credibility with at-risk individuals and communities were critical to success, supported by the city’s financial backing and operational autonomy.

source.name: Sam Stragand
source.publication: Poverty Solutions at the University of Michigan

stories.title: Letter from the Editor: Lights, camera, golden statuettes – how MLive’s news mission has led to film festival acclaim
stories.summary: MLive's video team has won multiple film festival awards for documentaries since 2024, including 'The Bridge Swim' which recently received the audience award for Best Michigan Short at the Hell's Half Mile Film and Music Festival. The documentary about an annual swim under the Mackinac Bridge blends journalistic storytelling with cinematic elements. The team's approach prioritizes finding compelling stories first, then considering festival potential, with upcoming showings at the East Lansing Film Festival.

stories.summary: LGBT Detroit opened a new health and wellness center on Detroit’s westside offering free mental health therapy, support groups, fitness classes, nutrition programming, PrEP medication, testing and screenings. stories.title: Library Network Expands with Saginaw's Joining

This marks the winding down of the Mid-Eastern Michigan Library Cooperative and enables reciprocal borrowing between the systems.

stories.title: Library of Michigan Funds Allocated for Qualified Services
stories.summary: The Library of Michigan will use collected fees to fund qualified services including document reproduction, conferences, and specialized equipment. Unexpended funds can be carried forward to the next fiscal year instead of lapsing to the general fund.

stories.title: Life after the game
stories.summary: Prince AyoOla, a football coach at Madonna University, emphasizes preparing student-athletes for life beyond sports by encouraging early career planning and academic focus. Drawing from his own experience as a former NAIA All-American, he mentors players to view football as a pathway to opportunities beyond the game, including education and long-term career success. The story highlights his philosophy of building relationships with athletes to help them transition effectively after their sports careers end.

stories.title: Life for Lansing Residents on Streets Amid Murders of Unhoused Men
stories.summary: A discussion about the challenges faced by Lansing residents living on the streets, particularly in the context of a series of murders targeting unhoused men. The story explores the safety concerns and systemic issues affecting this vulnerable population.

stories.title: Lifelong Detroit Lions fan selling massive collection after death of close friend
stories.summary: Dan Foster, a lifelong Detroit Lions fan, is selling his 36-year collection of memorabilia after the death of his close friend Gary Wayne Slatton. stories.title: Lightning-sparked Craig Lake fire half contained as 3 U.P. blazes burn
stories.summary: Three wildfires burning in rugged parts of Michigan’s Upper Peninsula are being fought with what the DNR calls 'steady progress.' The 434-acre Ridge Fire northwest of Marquette is 30% contained, with its cause still under investigation. Residents along North Basin Drive remain on 'ready' status, and drones are banned over fire zones.

stories.title: Meet the Michigan Supreme Court candidates: Jody White
stories.summary: Jody White, a real estate broker and former political candidate, is running for Michigan Supreme Court despite not meeting the state's legal licensing requirements. She argues for greater layperson representation in the judiciary and criticizes the current system as being dominated by legal professionals. The article includes her interview with Michigan Public, where she discusses her qualifications and views on judicial fairness.

stories.summary: Meijer has donated $1 million to support a nearly $25 million renovation and two-story expansion of the Kent District Library's Walker branch, set to open Oct. 19. The new facility will include children's programming areas, community meeting rooms, study spaces, a podcasting studio, and an esports room, driven by community feedback about outgrowing the existing library.

stories.title: Men charged with murder in Hazel Park shooting linked to Detroit stabbing
stories.summary: Three men—Brown, Clayborn-Marshall, and Dyer—have been charged with murder in a Hazel Park shooting linked to a Detroit stabbing. They were arraigned on September 5 and 29, with bond denied for all. A preliminary examination is scheduled for October 27. The Hazel Park Police Department is seeking public information about the case.

photo.alt: Men charged with murder in Hazel Park shooting linked to Detroit stabbing

stories.title: Men charged with murder in Hazel Park shooting linked to Detroit stabbing
stories.summary: Three Detroit men face first-degree murder charges in the August shooting death of 43-year-old Ryan Leslie Adams in Hazel Park, which investigators believe was retaliation for a fatal Detroit stabbing earlier that day. Terryon Anthony Brown (20), Dashawn Deonte Clayborn-Marshall (23), and Quintaz Eric Dyer (21) were denied bond and face charges including home invasion and armed robbery. A preliminary examination conference is scheduled for October 27.

stories.title: Mexican American Council’s ARPA funding compliance addressed by city leaders
stories.summary: Saginaw City Manager Tim Morales said an organization that received $620,000 in city-provided federal funds remains under compliance despite questions about the group’s eligibility. The Saginaw City Council approved multiple rounds of federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding for the Mexican American Council, including $500,000 in January 2023 and an additional $120,000 the following year. At the council’s Monday, Sept. 14 meeting, council members asked Morales for an update on the Mexican American Council’s status as an eligible recipient of the money. Media reports last week questioned the organization’s eligibility to receive ARPA funds as well as its status as a nonprofit.

stories.title: Michigan advocates work to ease election security anxieties as Nov. 3 approaches
stories.summary: With two weeks remaining until the Nov. 3 general election, Michigan advocates and nonprofits are addressing election security concerns through outreach, legal protections, and transparency efforts. Experts emphasize the state's decentralized election system as a security safeguard while monitoring potential federal interference and mail-in voting challenges. Organizations like Common Cause and the Michigan Election Observation Project are deploying hotlines, observers, and educational campaigns to ensure voter confidence.

photo.alt: Michigan advocates work to ease election security anxieties as Nov. 3 approaches

stories.title: Michigan AG: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan’s ‘illegal monopoly’ violates antitrust laws
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel filed a federal lawsuit accusing Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan of violating antitrust laws through an 'illegal monopoly' and anticompetitive tactics that drive up healthcare costs. The lawsuit claims BCBSM's market dominance suppresses competition, forces providers to reduce services or exit the market, and inflates pricing for consumers. Nessel seeks damages and relief under the Sherman Act and Michigan Antitrust Reform Act.

stories.title: Michigan AG candidate Doug Lloyd cut charges, sought no jail in sex-crime cases
stories.summary: Republican Doug Lloyd is running for Michigan attorney general on his three decades of experience as a prosecutor. However, a Metro Times review of court records and case files found instances during his tenure as Eaton County prosecutor where cases involving sexual assault, child exploitation, and domestic violence resulted in reduced charges, probation instead of jail, or no prosecution. The findings emerge as Lloyd faces Democrat Eli Savit in a closely contested race to succeed term-limited Attorney General Dana Nessel.

photo.alt: Doug Lloyd, Michigan AG candidate
