stories.summary: $85,000.00 will be awarded to the Michigan Sheriffs’ Association for victim support and trainings.

stories.title: Michigan Smart Trade Alliance tracker shows over $26 billion in tariff-driven costs paid statewide
stories.summary: The Michigan Smart Trade Alliance has launched a tracker estimating Michigan households have incurred over $26 billion in tariff-related costs since January 2025, or about $6,419 per household. The estimate uses data from the National Taxpayers Union Foundation, though other analysts and the White House provide lower figures. The alliance advocates for ending trade policies they claim raise costs and hinder economic planning.

photo.alt: Michigan Smart Trade Alliance tracker shows over $26 billion in tariff-driven costs paid statewide

stories.title: Michigan Spill Prompts Federal Probe of Energy Transfer Pipelines' Safety
stories.summary: A recent crude oil spill in Michigan has triggered a federal investigation into Energy Transfer's pipeline safety practices, focusing on the use of steel encirclement sleeves that may interfere with leak detection. The spill, which occurred near a residential area, was reported by a member of the public and required cleanup efforts by state officials. The PHMSA ordered Energy Transfer to inventory all repair sleeves and address integrity risks, following concerns about similar failures in Pennsylvania and North Carolina.
entities: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Director to Ensure Expenditure of Fiscal Recovery Funds by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director must ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are expended by December 31, 2026. Funds at risk of lapsing after September 30, 2026, will be automatically reappropriated for the same purpose through December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Requires Expenditure of ARPA Funds by December 2026
stories.summary: The state budget director must ensure all American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds allocated to Michigan under Public Law 117-2 are fully expended by December 31, 2026. Funds that would otherwise lapse after September 30, 2026, are automatically reappropriated for the same purpose until the deadline.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Complete Space Utilization Assessment by July 1
stories.summary: The Michigan state department is required to complete a space utilization assessment by July 1 using a form developed by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget. The assessment will cover all space assigned under building occupancy agreements and leased office locations, with plans to optimize space usage.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Prioritize State-Owned Facilities in Space Optimization
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must develop a plan to reduce, consolidate, or optimize assigned space, prioritizing state-owned facilities. The plan must comply with space standards established by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget unless exceptions are approved.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Report on Federal Policy Impacts by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must submit a report by December 31, 2026, detailing federal guidelines, rules, or policy changes (including H.R. 1 and the Rural Health Transformation Program) that significantly impact its operations. The report will address changes in federal revenue and their effects on public health and welfare.

stories.title: Michigan State Files Antitrust Complaint Against Blue Cross for Anticompetitive Practices
stories.summary: The Michigan Attorney General alleges Blue Cross has engaged in anticompetitive conduct by suppressing healthcare provider reimbursements and inflating premiums, harming both consumers and providers. The complaint claims this behavior has degraded healthcare availability and quality across the state.

stories.title: Michigan State Files Antitrust Lawsuit Against Blue Cross Over Healthcare Practices
stories.summary: The State of Michigan alleges Blue Cross engaged in anticompetitive practices that reduced healthcare access, inflated costs, and worsened health outcomes for consumers. The lawsuit seeks damages and remedies under Michigan's Antitrust Reform Act and other statutes, including claims for monopolistic behavior in healthcare markets.

stories.title: Michigan State Fiscal Recovery Funds Expenditure Plan
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director is required to ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are spent by December 31, 2026. Unexpended funds after September 30, 2026 will be automatically reappropriated until that deadline. The act also outlines reallocation procedures for funds at risk of missing deadlines, including redirecting them to public health and safety employee payroll and benefits.

stories.title: Michigan state House committee hears testimony over concerns about ballot initiative process
stories.summary: A state House committee in Michigan is examining ways to improve the ballot initiative process after a conservative-backed measure failed to qualify for the ballot. Americans for Citizen Voting (ACV) submitted over 700,000 signatures but was disqualified due to insufficient valid signatures, with the group criticizing delays and lack of transparency in the review process. The committee emphasized it is focused on procedural improvements rather than political outcomes.

stories.title: Michigan State University shifts to online classes after power outage

The outage began when a central connection point at the T.B. Simon Power Plant failed, prompting university leaders to reduce strain on systems while crews work to restore services. stories.summary: The Michigan Strategic Fund revised incentives for battery maker Our Next Energy, reducing state funding from $200 million to $150 million and adjusting job commitments and timelines. The fund also expanded a program to support auto parts suppliers in transitioning to EV and diversified supply chains.

Kuilema's lawyer argued the case could set a precedent affecting future discrimination claims, while Calvin's attorney maintained the firing was not based on Kuilema's own protected characteristics. Crumbley, who pleaded guilty in 2022 to four murders and seven injuries, had his appeal to withdraw his guilty plea denied in May 2025 for lacking merit. His attorney argued that waiving appellate rights by pleading guilty deprived him of a direct appeal.

stories.title: Michigan traffic stops are leading to deportations
stories.summary: A 2025 traffic stop in Brownstown Township led to a driver's arrest by federal agents after a local officer called Border Patrol to 'validate' a foreign license. This highlights how Michigan's driver's license law, which requires valid immigration status, contributes to deportations for minor traffic violations. Despite advocates' efforts, a 2025 bill to expand license eligibility for migrants failed, with lawmakers citing concerns about state security and unauthorized immigration. An investigation found 388 instances since 2021 where local police reported migrants to Border Patrol for minor infractions.

stories.title: Mollusk microbiome? It’s all in the family
stories.summary: University of Michigan researchers found that mollusk microbiomes are determined more by species taxonomy than environmental factors. The study reviewed 85 studies and found that members of the same species have more similar microbiomes regardless of location, while different species in the same environment have distinct microbiomes. This has implications for understanding mollusk resilience to environmental changes.

stories.title: NASA astronaut Christina Koch takes new space agency role
stories.summary: NASA astronaut Christina Koch, who holds the record for the longest spaceflight by an American woman at 328 days, has taken on a new role within the agency. Koch, a North Carolina State University graduate, previously served as a flight engineer on the International Space Station during Expeditions 59, 60, and 61, including the historic first all-female spacewalk in 2019.

photo.alt: NASA astronaut Christina Koch takes new space agency role

stories.title: NASA astronaut Christina Koch trades in spacesuit for desk job
stories.summary: Grand Rapids native and NASA astronaut Christina Koch is transitioning to a new role as acting deputy chief engineer at NASA, effective Nov. 1, 2026. This marks her shift from active spaceflight assignments to management, following the retirement of Katherine Van Hooser. Koch, who recently participated in the Artemis II mission and holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman, will leverage her technical and operational expertise in her new position.

stories.title: National average gas price hits $4.33 per gallon as of Oct. 15, 2026
stories.summary: The national average gas price reached $4.33 per gallon on October 15, 2026, according to AAA Fuel Prices data. State prices ranged from $3.704 in North Carolina to $6.237 in California, with Michigan averaging $4.579. The report provides a detailed breakdown of regular gasoline prices across all 50 states.

stories.title: ‘Natural’ American cheese? Midwest company says it’s made it
stories.summary: Sargento has developed a 'natural' American cheese in response to federal nutrition guidance urging reduced consumption of highly processed foods. The company aims to provide a lower-ingredient alternative to traditional processed cheese while appealing to both existing cheese consumers and those who have moved away from American cheese. Executives emphasize transparency in labeling and positioning the product alongside processed options to invite a broader audience.

stories.title: Near Sleeping Bear Dunes, residents battle beavers — and feds — over floods
stories.summary: Residents around Little Traverse Lake in Leelanau County blame beaver dams for recurring flooding that damages properties. The National Park Service only permits dam removal after water levels peak, but residents argue this is too late to prevent damage. A $1.1 million culvert project and studies show dam removal can significantly lower lake levels, yet the park maintains a cautious approach requiring data-driven justification for interventions.

photo.alt: A beaver dam

stories.title: Negative Space at Detroit Artists Market: An Exhibition of Unrealized Public Sculpture
stories.summary: Negative Space is an exhibition at Detroit Artists Market exploring unrealized public sculptures through maquettes, renderings, and documentation. Curated by Veronica Bielat, it highlights how public space is shaped by both realized and rejected works, featuring artists like Foster Willey, Lois Teicher, and Richard Bennet whose proposals never materialized but demonstrate artistic process and resilience.

stories.title: Neighborhood Theatre Group to present Halloween-season Black Cat show

stories.title: Nessel discusses threats of federal monitors, law enforcement at polling places during voter forum
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel addressed federal threats to election processes during a voter forum in Washington, D.C., emphasizing preparations for potential federal interventions at polling places and the impact on local election officials. She highlighted Michigan's decentralized election system and efforts to combat misinformation and threats against election workers, alongside fellow Democrats from California and Maine.

photo.alt: Nessel discusses threats of federal monitors, law enforcement at polling places during voter forum

stories.title: Nessel files federal antitrust lawsuit against Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel filed a federal antitrust lawsuit against Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan, alleging the company violated state and federal laws through anti-competitive agreements. The lawsuit claims these practices have stifled competition, led to higher insurance premiums, and reduced healthcare provider payments, harming both state employees and general policyholders. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan called the allegations unfounded, stating it disagrees with the characterization of an uncompetitive market.

stories.title: Nessel joins lawsuit seeking consumer protections as chatbot service declares bankruptcy
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel joined 38 other states and the District of Columbia in a lawsuit against Character.AI after the chatbot service filed for bankruptcy. The platform faces scrutiny over privacy and safety concerns, including a 2024 wrongful death lawsuit linked to a chatbot's alleged role in a teen's suicide. The lawsuit highlights issues like chatbots posing as licensed professionals, exposure of minors to explicit content, and failure to comply with privacy laws.

She emphasized the state's decentralized election processes and preparedness through units like hate crimes investigations and briefings for local law enforcement.

stories.summary: The University of Michigan celebrated the start of Latine Heritage Month with an event themed 'Lo Futuro' at the Michigan Union. Keynote speaker Curtis Acosta emphasized preserving cultural traditions through art and criticized policies affecting Latine communities. The event highlighted the resilience of Latine heritage and called for solidarity and liberation.

stories.summary: A new indoor play space and cafe called The Grove has opened in Ann Arbor, founded by three brothers with young children. The facility features play areas for different age groups, a cafe serving coffee and kid-friendly drinks, and party rental options. The business aims to provide a safe, family-friendly environment where parents can relax while their children play.

stories.title: New bills would require Michigan utilities to pay customers for long outages
stories.summary: Senate Democrats introduced bills requiring Michigan utilities to pay outage credits to customers after outages exceeding 72 hours or four annual outages. The bills aim to discourage prolonged outages and bar utilities from recouping credits through rate hikes, following storms that left 300,000+ households without power.

stories.summary: A 46-year-old New Boston woman was sentenced to five years in federal prison after pleading guilty to a multimillion-dollar fraud scheme involving fictional child modeling events. The scheme defrauded victims of $4.6 million through fake modeling opportunities.

stories.title: New Deepfake Resilience Hub combats rise of AI-generated misinformation
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's new Michigan Deepfake Resilience Hub (M-DRH) aims to help the public detect and understand AI-generated misinformation. Led by Khalid Malik, the initiative addresses gaps in deepfake detection tools for everyday users and includes a public verification portal, training programs, and policy guidance. The project was selected for a grant from the University's Strategic Initiative Fund, a $1 billion investment over 10 years.

stories.summary: The Detroit Historical Society’s 'This is 100: America’s Thanksgiving Parade' exhibit showcases the parade’s history from its 1924 debut through modern times, featuring artifacts, costumes, and interactive elements. stories.summary: A new resiliency center in Grand Blanc, Michigan, opened to provide healing and emotional support following a 2025 church shooting and fire. The event aims to foster conversations about supporting those affected by trauma.

stories.title: New health clinic bringing medical, pharmacy services to Burton and Flint’s East Side
stories.summary: A new health clinic, Hamilton East Clinic, is set to open on Sept. 28, 2026, in Burton, offering medical, behavioral health, and pharmacy services. The clinic aims to improve healthcare accessibility for residents in Burton and Flint’s East Side, who have had limited local options. It will operate Monday through Friday with a drive-through pharmacy and plans to collaborate with community organizations.

stories.title: New House committee to examine signature verification sampling process for ballot initiatives
stories.summary: A new select committee in the Michigan House was established to review the signature verification sampling process for ballot initiatives, following a deadlock on a voter ID petition. The committee, led by Republicans, aims to ensure the process is followed correctly and address concerns about potential partisan bias in the Board of State Canvassers' decisions.

stories.title: New ‘Kids Count’ data shows drop in college readiness, education participation among young adults
stories.summary: The Michigan League for Public Policy's 2026 Kids Count report shows declining college readiness and education participation among young adults, with Michigan ranking 42nd nationally in education. The report highlights increased poverty rates for children, drops in Medicaid and SNAP enrollment, and rising food insecurity, while noting an 84% increase in youth voter turnout since 2016.

stories.title: New land purchases will advance Ann Arbor's Treeline Trail plan
stories.summary: Recent and upcoming land purchases in Ann Arbor are expected to become major parts of the planned Treeline Trail, which will run along Allen Creek. The City Council will vote to purchase a lot on Felch Street, and the Treeline Conservancy is finalizing design negotiations for the trail's construction. The trail will include an elevated section with a signature bridge over Main Street.

stories.title: New Meijer Store Comes to 5 Mile and Beck
stories.summary: A new 159,000-square-foot Meijer supercenter opened September 30 on Five Mile Road in Plymouth Township, featuring expanded services including a drive-thru pharmacy, garden center, and pet department. The 21-acre development also includes an updated gas station with EV charging stations that opened September 2. The site was previously a contaminated prison that required $15 million in cleanup under Michigan Act 381.

stories.title: New Michigan laws crack down on gift card fraud
stories.summary: Gift card fraud happens when someone takes a card, steals the redemption information, and puts it back on the shelf. Fraudsters can steal the balance of the card before the purchaser can use it.

stories.title: New Natural Resources Commission appointee draws criticism
stories.summary: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer’s nominees for the Natural Resources Commission, including DTE Energy executive Trevor Lauer and conservationist George Lindquist, face criticism over potential conflicts of interest and shifting priorities. Lauer’s ties to DTE Energy, a company often criticized for rising electricity rates and data center support, have raised concerns about conservation priorities, while Lindquist’s conservation background is praised by peers. Both nominees, if approved by the Senate, would begin terms in January 2027.

stories.title: New Natural Resources Commission appointee draws criticism

Lauer's nomination, alongside conservationist George Lindquist, requires Senate approval to begin terms in 2027. Critics highlight DTE Energy's controversies over electricity rates and data center advocacy as conflicting with conservation priorities.

Owner Omar Linder emphasized the community's welcoming support and the restaurant's focus on R&B music and future bar plans. The menu includes five spice levels, gourmet coney dogs, and a mural honoring Linder's late friend Alberto Allen.

stories.title: New pipe repair method lets homeowners skip the dig
stories.summary: Homeowners facing damaged sewer lines can now opt for a less invasive repair method called sewer lining, which avoids the need for excavation. Marcus Piwonski of Hoover Electric, Plumbing, Heating and Cooling explains that the technique uses a felt-type liner inverted into existing pipes, creating a new pipe within the old one. This method spares homeowners the disruption of digging and is recommended for early detection of issues through camera inspections.

stories.title: New program from Warren police, Turning Point Macomb aims to break cycle of domestic violence
stories.summary: The Warren Police Department has partnered with Turning Point Macomb to launch Operation Cycle Break, a program connecting domestic violence survivors with immediate resources during police responses. The initiative coincides with Domestic Violence Awareness Month and aims to provide support through collaboration between law enforcement and advocacy organizations.

stories.summary: Ali Mohsini opened Rumi’s Garden in Grand Rapids to honor Afghan culture and the teachings of poet Rumi. stories.title: New state rules restrict wireless devices in schools, free meals provided

stories.title: New Ypsi farmers and gardeners added to library’s oral history project
stories.summary: The Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Project has expanded with 12 new narrators and 11 oral histories, focusing on BIPOC, Indigenous, younger, immigrant, and refugee growers in the Ypsilanti area. The project documents their stories about food sovereignty, cultural legacy, and community resilience, including contributions from Anishinaabe seed-keeper Shiloh Maples and refugee advocate Phimmasone Kym Owens. A new community advisory board helped deepen representation, and the collection will be available through the Ypsilanti District Library until Sept. 28.

stories.title: Newly counted ballots mean Hamtramck's mayor may have actually lost last year's election
stories.summary: Nearly a year after Hamtramck Mayor Adam Alharbi won his 2025 mayoral race by 11 votes, an additional 37 ballots discovered the day after the election were counted in October 2026, flipping the results to show challenger Muhith Mahmood winning by 12 votes. Legal challenges remain pending, including Alharbi's claim that Mahmood does not meet residency requirements and potential disputes over ballot legitimacy. The Wayne County Board of Canvassers will not certify Mahmood as winner until a residency hearing on October 22.

photo.alt: Members of the Wayne County Board of Canvassers consult with an elections official while overseeing the tabulation of 37 additional ballots from Hamtramck's 2025 municipal elections.

stories.title: NOAA predicts magnetic storm. Could northern lights shine?
stories.summary: Michigan could see strong northern lights on Thursday and Friday nights if NOAA's solar forecasts are accurate. The agency predicts a G1 or G2 geomagnetic storm with a Kp index up to 5 on Oct. 8, and a G2 storm watch for Oct. 9 due to a coronal mass ejection from an M1.4 flare. Clear conditions in dark sky areas would improve viewing chances, though clouds may hinder visibility in some northern regions.

stories.title: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan's Constitution: Here's How It Would Work
stories.summary: Michigan's constitution could be rewritten through a convention if voters approve Proposal 1. The process involves electing delegates, convening in October, and submitting proposed changes for approval. Historical records show the 1961 convention took 500 hours and generated over 800 proposals. A 2026 convention could cost $80 million, requiring legislative funding and addressing election logistics and delegate regulations.

photo.alt: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan's Constitution: Here's How It Would Work

stories.title: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan’s Constitution? Here’s how it would work
stories.summary: Michigan voters will decide in November 2026 whether to rewrite the state Constitution via Proposal 1. If approved, the measure would trigger a constitutional convention to elect 148 delegates who would draft a new constitution for voter approval. Supporters argue it could address government gridlock, while opponents warn it risks undoing recent voter-approved protections like abortion rights and redistricting reforms.

photo.alt: A historic photo of the delegates in a room at Michigan’s constitution convention.

stories.title: ‘She’s my biggest hero’: Detroit Lions player honors mom’s cancer battle
stories.summary: Detroit Lions defensive lineman Tyler Lacy honored his mother’s breast cancer battle during a Breast Cancer Awareness Month event in Dearborn. The event, part of the NFL’s Crucial Catch initiative, brought together survivors, healthcare providers, and local athletes to prepare care packages and promote cancer screenings. Lacy shared how his mother’s resilience inspired him and highlighted ACCESS Community Health’s efforts to improve cancer detection in underserved communities.

stories.title: She was supposed to care for her vulnerable uncle. Feds say Detroit woman misused his money instead

She faces legal charges and is scheduled for a preliminary hearing on October 1, 2026.

stories.title: 'Shoot every person in there': Man accused of threatening crowd at Holly restaurant reopening
stories.summary: Daniel James Gibson, 26, was charged with making a false report or threat of terrorism after allegedly threatening to shoot people at Andy’s Place’s Oct. 10 reopening celebration in Holly. Police reported Gibson attempted to bring alcohol to the event, climbed a fence after being removed, and threatened attendees while reaching into his backpack. He was arrested near Crapo Park with alcohol and a large knife, though no gun was found.

stories.title: Six species added to Michigan’s invasive plant lists following MI Commission of Ag & Rural Development vote
stories.summary: The Michigan Commission of Agriculture and Rural Development approved adding six invasive plant species to Michigan’s restricted and prohibited lists. Four species will be restricted, effective January 1, 2028, while two will be prohibited, effective June 19, 2026. The decision followed a public comment period and scientific review, with over 2,000 responses, 90% in favor.

stories.title: Slotkin, bipartisan group of lawmakers introduce bill to improve ovarian cancer prevention and care
stories.summary: U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin introduced a bipartisan bill to expand access to ovarian cancer prevention and care, including genetic counseling, testing, and improved access to gynecologic oncology specialists. The legislation, cosponsored by Republican Sen. Katie Britt, was introduced on Sept. 24 and aims to address barriers to early detection and treatment, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Slotkin highlighted her personal connection to the issue, having lost her mother and grandmother to ovarian cancer.

stories.title: Social Security COLA could be largest in 4 years: Is it enough?
stories.summary: Tens of millions of Social Security recipients are on track for a 3.5% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027, the highest increase in four years. stories.title: Some residents evacuate as fire crews continue battling Upper Peninsula wildfires
stories.summary: Firefighters in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula are battling two wildfires in Marquette and Baraga counties that prompted three evacuations over the weekend. The Craig Lake Fire and Ridge Fire, first spotted by a DNR pilot on October 9, have burned 30 and 256 acres respectively. Authorities have established an evacuation center and are using aircraft to suppress the fires, which are fueled by dry conditions and high winds. The cause remains under investigation.

stories.title: SOS Community Services Advocates for Rapid Re-Housing Amid Federal Policy Shifts
stories.summary: SOS Community Services' Executive Director Rhonda Weathers discusses the success of Rapid Re-Housing in helping families achieve housing stability, the potential impact of federal policy changes phasing out the model, and factors contributing to rising homelessness in Washtenaw County. stories.summary: University of Michigan students and community members gathered for an event hosted by LSA senior Larnell Gross to showcase his book, which uses 11 books published by the University of Michigan Press to highlight minority groups and historical civil rights movements in the United States. The event, part of the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, featured free online access to selected books and a public archive visit. Gross aims to make academic texts and American history more accessible through creative formats and free digital resources.

stories.title: South Lyon city council directs staff to examine impacts of canceling Flock contract
stories.summary: South Lyon city council has directed staff to assess the implications of canceling its contract with Flock, an automated license plate reader company, following significant resident opposition. Concerns include privacy risks, data misuse, and the potential for surveillance overreach, with residents emphasizing the need for legal guardrails and transparency. Community members highlighted the dangers of data breaches and the ethical issues surrounding perpetual tracking.

photo.alt: South Lyon city council directs staff to examine impacts of canceling Flock contract

stories.title: South Lyon City Council votes to cover cameras, end contract with Flock
stories.summary: South Lyon City Council members voted 5-2 to terminate their contract with Flock Safety, ending the use of automated license plate reader cameras. The resolution requires the police department to stop using data from the cameras and cover the devices located along 10 Mile Road. The decision followed resident concerns about data privacy and Fourth Amendment issues after the cameras were installed in November 2025.

photo.alt: Flock license plate reader camera in South Lyon

stories.title: South Lyon City Council votes to cover cameras, end contract with Flock
stories.summary: South Lyon City Council voted 5-2 to terminate its contract with Flock Safety, covering two automated license plate reader cameras and discontinuing data access. The resolution prohibits police from using or sharing data obtained through the cameras, except as required by law. The decision followed resident concerns about data privacy and Fourth Amendment issues.

stories.title: Speakeasy, sports complex, beer garden envisioned for historic Michigan paper mill
stories.summary: The former Plainwell Paper Mill, vacant for 26 years, has been transformed into the Michigan Classic Auto Mill with plans for an underground speakeasy, restaurant, beer garden, and indoor sports complex. Owners Darius and Rimante Grigaliunas, along with realtor Ryan Irons, are seeking tenants to fill remaining spaces in the 255,000-square-foot building. The project includes a Hot Rod Cafe, kayak rentals, and community-focused businesses, following the couple's previous restoration of the Wurlitzer Piano plant in Illinois.

photo.alt: Tony Knight looks at a classic car with his friend, Tim Girardin, during the grand opening of the Michigan Classic Auto Mill in Plainwell, Michigan on Oct. 3, 2026.

stories.title: Speaker Mike Johnson talks Iran, public safety with Tom Barrett in Michigan 7th campaign stop
stories.summary: U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson joined Republican Rep. Tom Barrett in Mason, Michigan, to discuss public safety and Iran policy during Barrett's campaign for the 7th Congressional District. The event featured endorsements from law enforcement groups and highlighted Barrett's opposition to defunding police, contrasting with Democratic nominee Will Lawrence's past statements. Johnson criticized Lawrence as a 'communist' and emphasized retaining Barrett to continue Trump's agenda.

stories.title: Spirit Halloween Opens at Briarwood Mall in Ann Arbor
stories.summary: Spirit Halloween has opened at Briarwood Mall in Ann Arbor, occupying the former Forever 21 space. The national Halloween retailer sells costumes, decorations, and seasonal items.

photo.alt: Spirit Halloween Opens at Briarwood Mall in Ann Arbor

stories.title: Spirit of Detroit given to immigrant business leader
stories.summary: Mohammed Abdul Muhit, an immigrant business leader, received a Spirit of Detroit award for his work with the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation and community engagement. He has served as a District 3 Business Liaison and previously worked in Banglatown neighborhood initiatives.

photo.alt: Spirit of Detroit given to immigrant business leader

stories.title: Spotted lanternfly confirmed in Berrien County
stories.summary: A population of spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) has been confirmed in Berrien County. Although this detection was not found in a vineyard, MSU Extension urges producers in the area to remain vigilant and alert for spotted lanternfly.

photo.alt: Spotted lanternfly confirmed in Berrien County

stories.title: Springfield Township Voters Approve Public Safety Millages
stories.summary: Springfield Township voters approved the renewal of police and fire millages. The 2-mill fire millage passed with 61.31% in favor, and the 2.9441-mill police millage, funded by the Oakland County Sheriff's Office, was supported by 55.46% of voters. Both measures are set for a 10-year term.

photo.alt: St. Mary's Episcopal in Orion

stories.title: Emily Slomovits & Friends
stories.summary: Emily Slomovits, who began playing violin at seven and performing with her family duo Gemini from age eight, has expanded her musical repertoire to include jazz, folk, and classical styles. Now in her early teens, she performs solo, with Gemini, and in various groups, showcasing her versatility across string quartets, folk, and country bands. The event will take place at The Ark.

stories.title: Jackopierce
stories.summary: The Ark announces ticket pricing details for Jackopierce's upcoming event. Online/phone purchases include MUTO's processing fee, while in-person purchases at The Ark during box office hours are available without fees. The event features Jack O’Neill and Cary Pi.

stories.title: Bonnie "Prince" Billy
stories.summary: Ticket prices on The Ark's website include all-in pricing for online or phone purchases, incorporating the ticket price and MUTO’s processing fee. Tickets can be bought without fees in person at The Ark during box office hours.

stories.title: Mike Dawes
stories.summary: Mike Dawes, an English guitarist known for composing, arranging, and performing multiple parts simultaneously on a single guitar, is regarded as one of the world’s most creative modern fingerstyle guitarists. His repertoire includes original viral videos, popular arrangements, and mainstream chart success performing with Justin Hayward of The Moody Blues.

stories.title: Alash
stories.summary: Alash are masters of traditional Tuvan instruments and throat singing, blending ancient techniques with western elements to create a unique style that honors their heritage while evolving traditional music.

stories.title: St. Clair Shores covers 12 Flock cameras after residents raise privacy concerns
stories.summary: St. Clair Shores City Council voted to cover 12 Flock surveillance cameras following resident concerns about privacy and data misuse. The council will revisit the city's contract with Flock in March 2027. The cameras, used to track vehicle entries, were funded through the Drug Law Enforcement Fund at an annual cost of $3,000 per camera.

photo.alt: Covered Flock surveillance cameras in St. Clair Shores. (Copyright 2026 by WDIV ClickOnDetroit - All rights reserved.)

stories.title: Stabbing outside Buddy’s Pizza near Comerica Park leaves man in serious condition; suspect arrested
stories.summary: A man in his 30s was hospitalized in serious condition after being stabbed outside a Buddy’s Pizza restaurant near Comerica Park in Detroit on October 9. The incident occurred around 4 p.m. in the 1500 block of Broadway. A suspect, a man in his 20s, was arrested at the scene and taken to the Detroit Detention Center.

photo.alt: Stabbing outside Buddy’s Pizza near Comerica Park leaves man in serious condition; suspect arrested

stories.title: Staff Attorney
stories.summary: The Detroit Justice Center is hiring an attorney to help advance the legal nonprofit’s mission of criminal justice reform and civil rights advocacy. The full-time hybrid position pays a salary of $85,000-$95,000 plus benefits, with a start date of Sept. 1. Apply now.

photo.alt: Cydni Elledge, Documenters Community Practice 014

stories.title: Stakes high as police, fire millages return to Oakland County ballots
stories.summary: Highland Township is re-proposing a 2.32 mill fire millage with enhanced ballot language after an August failure, while Orion Township officials are hosting voter education events. Both communities face challenges in securing funding for emergency services amid rising costs and voter concerns about taxes. Supervisor Rick Hamill warns of potential service cuts if the millage fails again, and Orion's Chris Barnett emphasizes the non-negotiable nature of police and fire services.

photo.alt: Chris Barnett explaining funding with visual aids

stories.title: Starting the conversation: Center for American Dialogue opens
stories.summary: The University of Michigan’s Center for American Dialogue has launched with programming, events, and courses aimed at addressing societal divides through dialogue. The center offers in-person and online opportunities across multiple campuses and cultural centers, focusing on evidence-based practices to foster productive conversations and civic trust.

photo.alt: Starting the conversation: Center for American Dialogue opens

stories.title: State and People Sue Blue Cross for Antitrust Violations in Michigan Health Insurance Market
stories.summary: The State of Michigan and its citizens have filed a complaint against Blue Cross for anticompetitive practices, citing rising health insurance costs, insurer exits, and hospital unit closures due to declining reimbursements. The lawsuit aims to address the negative impacts on healthcare markets and the crisis faced by taxpayers and employers.

stories.title: State Appellate Defender Office to Support Resentencing Efforts
stories.summary: The Michigan State Appellate Defender Office will hire up to 14 limited term employees to support the financial impact of recent Supreme Court decisions requiring resentencing for individuals sentenced to life without parole for crimes committed at 19 or 20 years of age.

stories.title: State Boundary Commission Reviews Vevay Township Annexation on Oct. 7
stories.summary: The State Boundary Commission will review a request to annex land in Vevay Township into Mason City on October 7, as reported by Andrew Roth of WKAR. The annexation could facilitate a potential data center development.

photo.alt: Michigan Data Center Report

stories.title: State commits $89 million to clean up Detroit, Kalamazoo rivers
stories.summary: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer unveiled an $89-million 'Reclaiming the Rivers' program to address pollution in the Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers. Funds come from a Monsanto PCB settlement and a 2019 Kalamazoo sediment release settlement. $50 million targets Detroit River sediment, $25 million funds Kalamazoo watershed restoration, and $14 million creates a statewide fund.

photo.alt: Avatar photo

stories.title: State Files Antitrust Complaint Against Blue Cross for Alleged Anticompetitive Practices
stories.summary: The state alleges Blue Cross conspired with other Blue Cross and Blue Shield entities to limit competition in healthcare and insurance markets, resulting in harm to Michigan consumers and providers through anticompetitive practices. The complaint details horizontal agreements and license restrictions that suppressed competition nationwide.

stories.title: State Files Complaint Against Blue Cross for Anticompetitive Practices
stories.summary: The State of Michigan alleges Blue Cross's anticompetitive practices have limited consumer choices, driven up healthcare costs, and harmed the state's economy. These practices include agreements with other insurers to allocate customers, resulting in higher premiums and reduced provider access for taxpayers, public employees, and individuals.

stories.title: State Fiscal Recovery Funds Expenditure Deadline Enforced
stories.summary: The state budget director must ensure all American Rescue Plan Act funds are spent by December 31, 2026. Funds not used by September 30, 2026, will be automatically reappropriated for the same purpose until the deadline.

stories.title: State Fiscal Recovery Funds Must Be Expended by December 31, 2026 with Automatic Reappropriation
stories.summary: The state budget director must ensure all American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds are spent by December 31, 2026. Funds not used by September 30, 2026, are automatically reappropriated for their original purpose through December 31, 2026.

stories.title: State Fiscal Recovery Funds Must Be Expended by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The state budget director is required to ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are fully spent by December 31, 2026. Funds not used by September 30, 2026, will be automatically reappropriated for the same purpose through December 31, 2026.

stories.title: State House Committee Examines Ballot Initiative Process in Michigan
stories.summary: A state house committee is examining ways to improve the ballot initiative process in Michigan. Monday's hearing came after a measure backed by conservatives failed to make the ballot.

photo.alt: Lee Chatfield

stories.title: State House Committee hears testimony over concerns about ballot initiative process
stories.summary: The group Americans for Citizen Voting (ACV) testified before a state House committee about delays and lack of transparency in the ballot initiative process. ACV submitted over 700,000 signatures for a voter ID amendment but was denied due to insufficient valid signatures. The hearing focused on improving the process, with Republicans alleging bias against conservative groups and Democrats calling the proposed amendment 'voter suppression.'

photo.alt: The group Americans for Citizen Voting (ACV) took its concerns about the state ballot initiation approval process to the state House Monday.

stories.title: State is focused on literacy, but results are down
stories.summary: Michigan's reading scores have declined, prompting state officials and political candidates to address the issue. Governor Gretchen Whitmer prioritizes literacy in her final year, while candidates Jocelyn Benson and John James blame each other for the failing education system. New laws aim to improve reading instruction and teacher training, but challenges remain.

photo.alt: State is focused on literacy, but results are down

stories.title: State of Michigan asking people to submit their questions about infrastructure in survey
stories.summary: The Michigan Infrastructure Council wants to develop a Citizens Infrastructure Guide to help people understand the need to invest in road, water, internet, electricity and other essential services.

photo.alt: Macomb County to install two inflatable bladders into pipe to help reduce combined sewer overflows into Lake St. Clair

stories.title: State of Michigan Files Lawsuit Against Healthcare Provider Over Healthcare Access
stories.summary: The State of Michigan, led by Attorney General Dana Nessel, has filed a lawsuit against a healthcare provider in the Eastern District of Michigan. The case alleges impaired access to affordable and effective healthcare for Michigan residents, with Blue Cross serving as the third-party administrator for the plan. The lawsuit asserts proper venue in the district due to the defendant's business operations and the events giving rise to the claims.

stories.title: State of Michigan Sues Blue Cross for Anticompetitive Practices and Inflated TPA Fees
stories.summary: The State of Michigan and its residents are suing Blue Cross for anticompetitive practices that allegedly led to inflated TPA fees and reduced health insurance market competition. The lawsuit claims Blue Cross was unjustly enriched by receiving supracompetitive fees from the state and Michigan employers/consumers, and seeks restitution for these excess payments. The state is also acting as parens patriae to redress economic harm to Michigan's health insurance market participants.

stories.title: State of the Arts program brings U-M faculty artists to communities across the state
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's State of the Arts program, launched by the Arts Initiative, brings U-M faculty artists to communities across Michigan through workshops and events. The Faculty Art Ambassador program features artists like Catie Newell and Jonathan Holland, who engage with diverse audiences, including incarcerated individuals and youth in underserved areas, to foster creativity and community connections.

photo.alt: Artwork from a workshop taught by Catie Newell. Photo courtesy of Catie Newell.

stories.title: State police arrest man for stolen gun, suspected cocaine after report of shots fired
stories.summary: State police arrested a man and seized two firearms, including a stolen 9mm Glock pistol equipped with an automatic-conversion device, while investigating a report of shots fired on Sept. 19 in Muskegon, MI.

photo.alt: State police arrest man for stolen gun, suspected cocaine after report of shots fired

stories.title: State police arrest man for stolen gun, suspected cocaine after report of shots fired
stories.summary: Michigan State Police arrested a 22-year-old Muskegon man and seized a stolen 9mm Glock pistol with an automatic-conversion device, an unregistered AR-style rifle, and suspected cocaine packaged for sale after investigating a report of shots fired on Sept. 19. The suspect faces potential charges including possession of a stolen firearm, automatic-conversion device, and cocaine distribution.

photo.alt: State police arrested a man and seized guns and suspected cocaine after investigating a report of shots fired in Muskegon. (Provided by Michigan State Police)

stories.title: State police investigating officers fatally shooting armed man in Metro Detroit
stories.summary: Michigan State Police are assisting in an investigation of Redford Township officers who fatally shot an armed man near Beech Daly and Schoolcraft roads. The incident occurred when officers responded to a vehicle blocking the road and encountered a man with a handgun who failed to comply with their orders. The man was shot, transported to a hospital in stable condition, and officers involved have been placed on administrative leave pending the investigation.

photo.alt: A Michigan State Police vehicle is seen in this MLive file photo

stories.title: State regulators approve 20-year DTE contracts for Google data center in Wayne County
stories.summary: State regulators have approved a 20-year electricity contract between DTE Energy and Google for a data center in Van Buren Township, Michigan. The agreement, tied to 'Project Cannoli,' requires Google to pay at least 80% of its electricity costs, shielding other DTE customers from project expenses. The deal aims to lower electricity costs for Michigan residents and businesses by sharing infrastructure improvements and clean energy investments.

photo.alt: Image from the article

stories.title: State regulators approve nearly $140M rate hike for Consumers Energy natural gas customers
stories.summary: State regulators approved a $139.2 million annual natural gas rate increase for Consumers Energy, reducing the utility's original $240 million request by 42%. The 4.3% rate increase will take effect on Nov. 1, adding approximately $4 per month to customer bills. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel urged regulators to cut the request by more than half, citing concerns about inflated costs and unreasonable profit margins.

photo.alt: State regulators approve nearly $140M rate hike for Consumers Energy natural gas customers

stories.title: State Seeks Damages and Penalties Against Blue Cross for Antitrust Violations
stories.summary: The State of Michigan is seeking damages and penalties against Blue Cross for antitrust violations involving horizontal agreements that suppressed competitive pricing in healthcare services and reimbursements. The lawsuit includes requests for trebled damages under the Michigan Antitrust Reform Act, civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation, and costs/attorneys' fees.

stories.title: State Sen. Sean McCann Endorsed by Multiple Labor Organizations for Congress
stories.summary: State Sen. Sean McCann (D-Kalamazoo), the Democratic nominee for Michigan’s 4th Congressional District, was endorsed by a slate of labor organizations, including the Michigan AFL-CIO, UAW, AFT, MEA, SEIU, AFGE, AFSCME, CWA, IAFF/MPFFU, UA, SMART-TD, ATU, Michigan Building Trades, Michigan Carpenters, Teamsters Local 406, LIUNA Local 355, and UFCW Local 951.

photo.alt: State Sen. Sean McCann Endorsed by Multiple Labor Organizations for Congress

stories.title: State Senator Runestad Plans to Repeal Data Center Tax Exemptions
stories.summary: State Senator and Michigan Republican Party Chair Jim Runestad announced plans to introduce legislation repealing tax exemptions for data centers and their equipment. Runestad criticized tech conglomerates for leveraging Michigan's resources without transparency or community benefits.

photo.alt: State Senator Runestad Plans to Repeal Data Center Tax Exemptions

stories.title: State Senator Seeks to Repeal Data Center Tax Exemptions
stories.summary: State Senator and Michigan Republican Party Chair Jim Runestad announced plans to introduce legislation repealing tax exemptions for data centers and their equipment. Runestad criticized the current laws, stating that billion-dollar tech companies should pay taxes and provide benefits to Michigan residents. The proposed legislation aims to require transparency from data center operators seeking to operate in the state.

photo.alt: Michigan data center report graphic

stories.title: State Senator Supports Municipal Utility Proposal in Ann Arbor
stories.summary: State Sen. Jeff Irwin (D-Ann Arbor) endorses a municipal utility proposal, arguing it would reduce costs compared to DTE Energy. He cites lower bond rates for cities and data showing Michigan public utility customers paid 17% less per kilowatt-hour in 2024 than those served by investor-owned utilities. A 2026 report from the American Public Power Association also notes public power customers experienced 1.5 fewer hours without power in 2023.

photo.alt: Public power infrastructure

stories.title: State Sets Review of Annexation Request for Mason Data Center
stories.summary: The State Boundary Commission will review a request to annex land in Vevay Township into Mason, potentially enabling a data center to connect to city utilities.

photo.alt: State Sets Review of Annexation Request for Mason Data Center

stories.title: State Street and Warwick intersection in Saginaw to close Tuesday
stories.summary: Michigan Department of Transportation officials will close the State Street (M-58) and Warwick Street intersection Tuesday, Sept. 29, for grading and curb work. The intersection work is part of a larger effort to rebuild about one mile of eastbound State Street from Avalon Ave. to Bay Road.

photo.alt: Construction zone

stories.title: State will use $89 in settlements from polluters to clean up Kalamazoo, Detroit rivers
stories.summary: Michigan will use $89 million from pollution settlements with companies like Monsanto to clean up the Detroit and Kalamazoo Rivers. The funds will address decades of industrial contamination, restore fish habitats, and improve public riverfront access. The initiative, called Reclaim the Rivers, aims to leverage state spending to attract additional federal, local, and private funding.

photo.alt: Tree trunks embedded into the Kalamazoo River bank with roots facing outward to capture vegetation and sediment, creating habitat for aquatic life.

stories.title: States take Trump administration to court over weaker gas mileage standards
stories.summary: California, Michigan, and 24 others sued the Transportation Department over new fuel economy standards. They argue the 34.9 mpg target by 2031 ignores EV growth and hides $220B in forgone fuel savings. The administration claims the rules will lower vehicle costs but raise gasoline use and fuel costs over time.

stories.title: Statewide proposal for constitutional convention to appear on the ballot this November
stories.summary: This November, Michigan voters will decide on a proposal to convene a constitutional convention for a general revision of the state constitution. The question appears on the ballot every 16 years, with the last convention in 1962. Political science professor Joshua Koss and community members express mixed views on the potential impact of the convention, with concerns about partisanship and environmental policy risks.

stories.title: Statue of former Detroit Mayor Coleman A. Young to be instated at U.S. Capitol
stories.summary: The Coleman A Young Foundation's efforts to install a statue of former Detroit mayor Coleman A. Young in the U.S. Capitol are nearing completion. The statue will replace a marble sculpture of Lewis Cass, a former Michigan governor who supported slavery. The Charles H. Wright Museum will host an event on October 20 to celebrate the announcement.

photo.alt: Statue of former Detroit Mayor Coleman A. Young to be instated at U.S. Capitol

stories.title: STEAM Park Gallery Inspires Next Generation of Scientists, Engineers, and Artists
stories.summary: The STEAM PARK gallery at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum features interactive mechanical exhibits like Window Maze, Airfoil, Propeller Chair, and a digital Roulette Curve. Designed to inspire future scientists and artists, the gallery includes a 17th-century-style interactive clock. The article was written by George Crane.

photo.alt: Interactive mechanical exhibits in STEAM PARK gallery

stories.title: STEAM Park
stories.summary: The STEAM PARK gallery at the Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum features interactive mechanical exhibits inspired by Jules Verne, including a digital Roulette Curve and a 17th-century multi-interactive clock, designed to inspire future scientists, engineers, and artists.

photo.alt: STEAM Park

stories.title: ‘Steel now in the ground:’ $120M Traverse City airport expansion making steady progress
stories.summary: Construction of the 68,000-square-foot Concourse B at Cherry Capital Airport in Traverse City, Michigan, is progressing steadily since breaking ground in April 2026. Steel has been installed, and the terminal is expected to open in spring 2028 as part of a $190 million expansion plan called 'Gates to the Future.'

photo.alt: Cherry Capital Airport - Concourse B construction

stories.title: Steering wheel communicates for better semi-autonomous driving performance
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Michigan have developed a steering wheel that communicates with drivers to improve semi-autonomous driving performance. The innovation aims to enhance safety and efficiency in vehicles that are not fully autonomous.

photo.alt: A steering wheel in a driving simulator designed to communicate with semi-autonomous systems.

stories.title: Sterling Heights man allegedly captured on doorbell camera abusing dog gets plea deal
stories.summary: A 24-year-old Sterling Heights man pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor animal cruelty charge after being captured on a neighbor's doorbell camera allegedly striking a dog multiple times. Bradley Allen, 26, will be sentenced on Nov. 23 and had a felony charge dismissed as part of the plea deal. Police credited community vigilance for the tip that led to his arrest.

stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft alumnus and township clerk, emphasizes the integrity of the election system and was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year. He advocates for maintaining election sanctity and encourages involvement in the democratic process through certification programs.

stories.title: Steward of Democracy
stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft alumnus and township clerk, emphasizes the integrity of the election system and his role in maintaining democratic processes. He was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year in September 2026 for his dedication to election accuracy and transparency. Siegrist encourages community involvement in elections and is pursuing certifications to further his expertise in election administration.

stories.title: Still not up to code: A Wayne County judge orders developer to place rent payments into trust
stories.summary: A Wayne County judge mandated that developer Gastón Muñoz place all rent collected for his Detroit properties into a court-approved trust. The order aims to ensure funds are used for home repairs as Muñoz works to bring 299 rental properties up to code, despite accumulating $460,000 in blight tickets.

stories.title: Stop the Data Center hosts data center teach-in for UMich community
stories.summary: Stop the Data Center organized a teach-in for the University of Michigan community to discuss data center-related issues. The event aimed to educate attendees on the topic and its implications for the university and broader community.

stories.title: Stop the Data Center hosts teach-in for UMich community
stories.summary: Over 40 University of Michigan staff, students, and Ypsilanti community members attended a teach-in hosted by Stop the Data Center to oppose the University’s planned Ypsilanti Township data center in collaboration with Los Alamos National Laboratory. Attendees raised concerns about environmental risks, health complications from toxic chemicals, and the lack of local benefits from the $850 million project. Presenters highlighted the data center as an extension of the military-industrial-academic complex and questioned the University’s commitment to community safety and transparency.

photo.alt: An audience is turned towards a woman speaking into a microphone at the front of the room.

The piece emphasizes how fall planting strengthens root systems and reduces runoff before winter.

stories.title: Stubborn Brother Pizza Bar opens in downtown Ann Arbor
stories.summary: Stubborn Brother Pizza Bar, located at 405 S. Main St. in downtown Ann Arbor, uses New York City water to create its signature pizza dough. The family-owned restaurant, operated by Grace Mancy, employs a five-day fermentation process and Roto-Flex ovens to achieve an authentic New York-style crust. The establishment offers affordable options like $3 student slices on Tuesdays and has received praise for its unique dough and generous portion sizes.

stories.title: Student Survey Transparency Requirements
stories.summary: Districts and intermediate districts must make student survey questions and results publicly available on their websites and notify parents and legal guardians of the surveys, which include any from local, state, or federal governments.

stories.title: Students call for divestment on anniversary of Oct. 7 attacks
stories.summary: More than 100 students participated in a walkout across the University of Michigan campus to mark three years since Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel, demanding the university divest from financial and academic ties with Israel. Organized by Students Allied for Freedom and Equality (SAFE), the protest included chants condemning Israel's military actions in Gaza and calls for institutional accountability. Speakers emphasized connections between Palestinian solidarity and broader U.S. social justice movements, while highlighting the power of student activism.

They also say an extension of the bike lanes on Division Street is long overdue. The Division Street Bikeway Extension Project is in two phases, with the first running from Catherine Street to the bridge. Council member Lisa Disch emphasizes the need for safer infrastructure to adapt to new residents and public amenities.

stories.title: Survey Shows Michigan Local Officials Doubt Data Centers' Worth

stories.title: Suspect arrested hours after mother, 7-year-old daughter shot on Detroit's east side

The incident stemmed from an argument over a fight between children, leading to the suspect forcing entry and firing shots that injured the woman and her daughter. Police Chief Todd Bettison stated the suspect was the father of one of the children involved in the earlier altercation.

Cruises run on the Harbor Princess with adjusted departure times based on sunset, and ticket prices range from $30 to $50 for adults, with free rides for children under 3. stories.title: Tariff impact on Michigan
stories.summary: Trump's aggressive tariffs aimed to boost Michigan's competitiveness but have cost consumers $26 billion ($6,419 per household) since 2025. Tariff revenue reached $233 billion, but Supreme Court refunds reduced federal gains. Manufacturing jobs grew 0.8% in Michigan while declining nationally.

photo.alt: Donald Trump speaking at the Detroit Economic Club.

stories.title: Tariffs and their impact
stories.summary: Trump's aggressive tariff policy aimed to boost Michigan's competitiveness. While manufacturing has expanded, Michigan consumers are paying $26 billion more for goods since January 2025 due to tariffs, averaging $6,419 per household. Tariff revenue reached $233 billion through late September, but Supreme Court refunds are reducing federal revenue.

Medicaid cuts could remove 171,000 Michiganders from coverage by 2028.

stories.title: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed continued academic growth in 2026 M-STEP results, with notable improvements in English and math across multiple grades compared to 2019. Eighth graders saw a 7.6 percentage point increase in English proficiency, while seventh graders improved by 6.8 percentage points in math. The district also reported gains in SAT benchmarks, with 35.1% of students meeting English standards and 15.7% in math, both up from 2019. stories.title: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results

The district has used funds from a $94.4 million literacy lawsuit settlement to hire academic interventionists and expand tutoring, though budget challenges loom as those funds expire. Chronic absenteeism has also declined since pandemic-era closures, contributing to better student outcomes.

stories.title: The secret act of kindness one Michigan teacher did that changed Terry Crews’ life forever
stories.summary: Michigan native Terry Crews credited his high school art teacher Dwight Eichelberg with changing his life by submitting his artwork for scholarships without telling him, leading to opportunities at Interlochen Arts Academy and Western Michigan University. Eichelberg, now 82 and a farmer in Linden, MI, recognized Crews' artistic talent in the 1980s and helped him overcome self-doubt about pursuing art as a Black student. Their bond endured through Crews' NFL and acting careers, including a 2015 surprise reunion in Flint.

stories.title: The skincare scheme that led to consumer complaints, lawsuits and a federal investigation
stories.summary: Mazal Group, a company accused of operating a 'predatory and systematically unfair' skincare enterprise, settled a Hawaii class action lawsuit after evidence revealed its direct control over store operations despite claims of being a mere distributor. The settlement requires Mazal Group and its owners to pay $650,000 of a $950,000 total restitution to 110 affected consumers, though the company denies wrongdoing. Court records showed Mazal dictated store policies, product exclusivity, and customer service protocols across its branded locations.

stories.title: The Trump administration tried to stop the national EV charging program. It’s kept rolling anyway
stories.summary: The Trump administration froze funding for the Biden-era National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, but court rulings have allowed some states to continue using the money. A Sierra Club report shows $94 million was spent in 2025 on EV charging projects, with Pennsylvania and Ohio leading in funding. Legal challenges and delays have left over 95% of the allocated $5 billion unspent, though states are urged to accelerate spending to meet infrastructure goals.

stories.title: Trinity Health layoffs expose the danger of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
stories.summary: Trinity Health in Livonia, Michigan announced 557 layoffs linked to federal Medicare and Medicaid cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). The law has already put 23 Michigan healthcare providers at risk and is projected to strip 171,000-355,000 residents of health coverage. Republican lawmakers including Senate candidate Mike Rogers and Michigan's congressional delegation supported the legislation despite its negative impacts.

photo.alt: Trinity Health layoffs in Livonia, Michigan

stories.title: Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Award 2024 for top 10% worldwide attractions
stories.summary: The museum won Tripadvisor’s 'Travelers’ Choice Award 2024', placing it in the top 10% of worldwide attractions based on millions of reviews.

stories.title: Troy neighborhood streets overwhelmed by cut-through traffic amid Rochester Road construction
stories.summary: Construction on Rochester Road in Troy has driven cut-through traffic into residential neighborhoods. The city is directing drivers to alternate routes as the west side closure is expected to last three weeks, with additional street closures starting October 12.

photo.alt: Troy neighborhood streets overwhelmed by cut-through traffic amid Rochester Road construction

stories.title: Trump administration revokes $810M approved by Congress for refugee aid and more
stories.summary: The Trump administration has revoked $810 million in refugee aid approved by Congress, among other actions. The decision impacts funding allocated for refugee support programs.

photo.alt: An unloaded Glock 19X handgun sits next to a magazine and 9 mm ammunition at a gun range. At least 13 states currently allow firearms on public college campuses.

stories.title: Trump Administration Rolls Back Power Plant Emission Rules
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will roll back rules governing power plant emissions, despite scientific consensus on climate change. Rachel Rothschild, an assistant professor at Michigan Law, discusses the implications of this decision.

photo.alt: Stateside podcast cover image

stories.title: Trump administration says developers, loggers can kill endangered species
stories.summary: The Trump administration’s top wildlife official issued a directive expanding rollbacks of endangered species protections, allowing developers and loggers to kill endangered animals if the activity’s purpose is not to kill them. Wildlife advocates warn this undermines the Endangered Species Act, creating loopholes for habitat destruction and accidental harm. Legal challenges and debates over the law’s interpretation are expected to intensify.

photo.alt: Endangered species and logging activities

stories.title: Trump Announces Russian Diesel Deal to Address Soaring US Fuel Prices
stories.summary: President Trump announced a deal with Russia to ship diesel to the US market after diesel prices surpassed $6 per gallon, aiming to alleviate fuel costs.

photo.alt: Image from WDET article

stories.title: Trump appoints committee to revive quest to remove Lisa Cook from Fed board
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has formed a White House committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, seeking evidence she made false statements on a mortgage form. The committee will hold a closed-door hearing on Nov. 5, two days after the midterm elections, following a Supreme Court ruling that blocked Trump's previous attempt to remove Cook from the Fed board. The investigation aims to meet the court's standard for cause to fire board members.

photo.alt: Trump appoints committee to revive quest to remove Lisa Cook from Fed board

stories.title: Trump approval sinks to new low in Fox News poll
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to a new low in Fox News polling, with 36% approval and 64% disapproval, as voters express dissatisfaction with his handling of inflation and the economy. The findings come ahead of November's midterm elections, with Democrats widening their advantage and Republicans facing voter frustration over economic concerns.

photo.alt: Portrait of Fernando Cervantes Jr.

stories.title: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed
stories.summary: Donald Trump has canceled a planned public execution, though concerns persist about precedents already set by his administration.

photo.alt: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed

stories.title: Trump DOJ uses case of Utah letter carrier to highlight allegations of voting fraud
stories.summary: The Trump Department of Justice highlighted a Utah letter carrier case to emphasize allegations of voting fraud, while a federal court blocked a Postal Service rule that aimed to affect election policies. The Supreme Court upheld the decision, arguing the rule was an attempt to influence elections rather than a modest mail regulation.

photo.alt: Trump DOJ uses case of Utah letter carrier to highlight allegations of voting fraud

stories.title: Trump heads West in latest swing to bolster GOP in rocky lead-up to midterms
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is campaigning in multiple states to support Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections, despite low approval ratings and ongoing controversies. His tour includes stops in Alaska, Arizona, Montana, and Georgia, with a focus on key Senate races and gubernatorial contests. The article also highlights federal investigations into Trump's use of taxpayer funds for campaign ads and his rhetoric targeting specific communities.

photo.alt: Photo by Getty images

stories.title: Trump launches campaign tour in GOP-friendly states ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Donald Trump has launched a campaign tour in GOP-friendly states as part of efforts to energize the Republican base ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The tour focuses on key battleground states where the party aims to maintain control of Congress.

photo.alt: Trump launches campaign tour in GOP-friendly states ahead of midterms

stories.title: Trump likes data centers. Congress seems stuck. The midterms could deliver a verdict.
stories.summary: The House passed a bill requiring states to consider data centers paying for electricity costs, but Senate action is stalled. Trump opposes restrictions, and the issue is a key topic in midterm races with bipartisan opposition to data centers.

photo.alt: Data centers, including the one pictured here in Boardman, Oregon, on May 18, 2026, have been built along the Columbia River Gorge during the last few years. (Photo by Jordan Gale/Oregon Capital Chronicle)

stories.title: Trump lowers fuel economy standards. Detroit automakers welcome change
stories.summary: The Trump administration has finalized new fuel economy standards that relax requirements for automakers, reducing the mandated mileage compared to previous projections. The change aligns with Trump’s campaign to roll back policies favoring electric vehicles, potentially increasing vehicle affordability but also exposing Americans to more pollution. The decision follows tensions with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, which impacted oil prices.

photo.alt: Donald Trump speaks during an event on fuel economy standards in the Oval Office of the White House, Dec. 3, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci, File)

stories.title: Trump PAC helps drive Michigan Senate race toward record spending
stories.summary: Michigan’s US Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is on pace to be the most expensive in state history, with over $205 million in disclosed spending and an additional $65 million in reserved ads through Election Day. Trump-aligned super PACs like Senate Leadership Fund and No Going Back have driven GOP spending to $59.3 million, while Democrats have spent $23 million in disclosed campaign funds and $43.8 million in ads, including dark money. The race remains competitive with El-Sayed leading polls by 3.5 points and the Cook Political Report rating it a toss-up.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed in a split image

stories.title: Trump PAC helps drive Michigan Senate race toward record spending
stories.summary: Michigan's U.S. Senate race between Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed is on track to be the most expensive in state history, with over $205 million in disclosed spending and an additional $65 million in reserved ads. The race includes significant contributions from dark money groups, which do not disclose their donors, and is being heavily influenced by Republican-aligned super PACs, including those linked to Donald Trump.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed in a split image

stories.title: Trump pressed states for info on millions of voters in the midterms. It’s mostly failed.
stories.summary: A federal judge declared illegal the Trump administration’s effort to obtain sensitive voter data from states for the midterms, ruling it violated the Privacy Act. The Justice Department had pressured or sued states to share voter rolls, which were then transferred to Homeland Security Investigations. At least 16 states provided data, but court rulings and legal challenges have largely blocked the initiative. The decision marks another legal defeat for the Trump administration ahead of the elections.

photo.alt: Photo by Getty Images

stories.title: Trump promised a swing district blitz. He's going to a lot of very red states
stories.summary: Analysis of Donald Trump's campaign strategy focusing on red states rather than competitive swing districts ahead of the 2026 elections.

stories.title: Trump pushes daylight saving; clocks expected to change
stories.summary: Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift marks the return to standard time and gives Americans an extra hour of sleep, while also bringing earlier sunsets and more morning daylight through the winter months.

photo.alt: Trump pushes daylight saving; clocks expected to change

stories.title: Trump renames Lake Ontario to Lake America. What does Ontario mean?
stories.summary: The article explains the historical and Indigenous origins of the names of three Great Lakes: Lake Superior (named by French settlers as 'Le Lac Superior' meaning upper lake), Lake Michigan (derived from the Indigenous name Michigami), and Lake Huron (named after the Huron-Wendat people, previously called 'La Mer Douce' by French settlers).

photo.alt: Trump renames Lake Ontario to Lake America. What does Ontario mean?

stories.title: Trump's clock plan could affect Halloween
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's proposal to make daylight saving time permanent could impact Halloween, potentially requiring trick-or-treaters to end activities earlier. While the House passed legislation for year-round daylight saving time, the Senate's recess until Sept. 14 and uncertainty about sufficient votes leave the issue unresolved before the Nov. 1 clock change.

photo.alt: Portrait of Saman Shafiq

stories.title: Two campaigning in what could be last treasurer election in Jackson
stories.summary: Two candidates are competing in what could be the final election for Jackson city treasurer. David R. Hammontree, a university professor, is challenging incumbent Nanette Muntin, appointed in 2025 after the death of former treasurer Martin Griffin. A November ballot proposal seeks to change the treasurer position from elected to city-council appointed, potentially ending voter elections for the role. The winner would complete Griffin’s term ending in 2028 with no guaranteed re-election opportunity.
entities: League of Women Voters of Michigan Education Fund

photo.alt: Jackson city treasurer race

stories.title: Two Michigan boys found safe in Ohio after father flees with children from Inkster home
stories.summary: Inkster officers, with assistance from Detroit Police and Michigan State Police, located two boys and their father in Norwalk, Ohio, after a search spanning two states. The father was found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, while the children were unharmed. Inkster police confirmed no ongoing community threat.

photo.alt: Two Michigan boys found safe in Ohio after father flees with children from Inkster home

stories.title: Two Michigan residents charged with making terrorist threats against state officials
stories.summary: Attorney General Dana Nessel announced charges against Alicia Choucair of Roseville and Anthony Dekinderen of Lake Orion for making terrorist threats against public officials. Choucair threatened a mosque and Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud, while Dekinderen sent threatening emails targeting Michigan Supreme Court members, Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson. Both face multiple felony charges with potential decades-long prison sentences.

photo.alt: Two Michigan residents charged with making terrorist threats against state officials

stories.title: Two Michigan Supreme Court candidates aren't eligible to serve. What if they win?
stories.summary: Two Michigan Supreme Court candidates, Thomas W. Howe and Jody White, are ineligible to serve but remain on the ballot. University of Detroit Mercy Law Professor Aman McLeod explains potential legal challenges and outcomes if they win, including quo warranto suits and possible vacancies. The Michigan Secretary of State’s office has not responded to questions about next steps.

photo.alt: Michigan Supreme Court building exterior

stories.title: Two Michigan tribes complete a 130-mile kayak voyage along Lake Michigan
stories.summary: Two Michigan tribes, the Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi and the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi, completed a 10-day, 130-mile kayak and canoe journey along Lake Michigan to reaffirm their ancestral friendship and connection to water. The 'Paddle to Pokagon' voyage, which began on October 3 and concluded on October 12 (Indigenous Peoples’ Day), included gatherings, cultural ceremonies, and environmental stewardship efforts. Tribal members emphasized the importance of preserving traditions and inspiring younger generations through ancestral waterways.
entities: Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi

photo.alt: Scenes from the 'Paddle to Pokagon' voyage, which reaffirms the longstanding friendship between the Nottawaseppi Huron Band and the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi in a traditional and sovereign way. (Photo/Skyla Jewell-Hammie)

stories.title: U-M alumna Maaza Mengiste named MacArthur Fellow
stories.summary: University of Michigan alumna Maaza Mengiste, a fiction writer and professor whose work explores the human toll of political conflict, has been named a 2026 MacArthur Fellow. The award, often called the 'genius grant,' provides $800,000 in unrestricted funding over five years. Mengiste is among 20 recipients selected for the 2026 fellowships.
